p0.original: Rent, considered as the price paid for the use of land, is naturally the highest which the tenant can afford to pay in the actual circumstances of the land. In adjusting the terms of the lease, the landlord endeavours to leave him no greater share of the produce than what is sufficient to keep up the stock from which he furnishes the seed, pays the labour, and purchases and maintains the cattle and other instruments of husbandry, together with the ordinary profits of farming stock in the neighbourhood. This is evidently the smallest share with which the tenant can content himself, without being a loser, and the landlord seldom means to leave him any more. Whatever part of the produce, or, what is the same thing, whatever part of its price, is over and above this share, he naturally endeavours to reserve to himself as the rent of his land, which is evidently the highest the tenant can afford to pay in the actual circumstances of the land. Sometimes, indeed, the liberality, more frequently the ignorance, of the landlord, makes him accept of somewhat less than this portion; and sometimes, too, though more rarely, the ignorance of the tenant makes him undertake to pay somewhat more, or to content himself with somewhat less, than the ordinary profits of farming stock in the neighbourhood. This portion, however, may still be considered as the natural rent of land, or the rent at which it is naturally meant that land should, for the most part, be let.
p0.zh: 租金被认为是为使用土地所支付的价格,当然是租户在土地实际情况中能够支付的最高租金。 在调整租赁条件时,房东尽量让他在农产品中所占的份额不超过他用来维持种子供应、支付劳动力、购买和保养牲畜和其他畜牧业工具的库存,以及附近农业库存的普通利润。 这显然是租户可以满足的最小份额,而不会成为失败者,房东也很少想离开他。 无论农产品的哪一部分,或同一件事,无论价格的哪一部分,都高于这一份额,他自然地努力将土地作为租金保留给自己,这显然是租户在土地的实际情况中能够支付的最高数额。 有时,房东的宽松性,更经常是无知,使他接受的比这部分略少;有时,尽管更罕见的是,房客的无知也使他承诺比邻里农庄的一般利润多一些,或满足于少一些。 然而,这一部分仍可视为土地的自然租金,或自然意味着土地大部分应当让与的租金。

p1.original: The rent of land, it may be thought, is frequently no more than a reasonable profit or interest for the stock laid out by the landlord upon its improvement. This, no doubt, may be partly the case upon some occasions; for it can scarce ever be more than partly the case. The landlord demands a rent even for unimproved land, and the supposed interest or profit upon the expense of improvement is generally an addition to this original rent. Those improvements, besides, are not always made by the stock of the landlord, but sometimes by that of the tenant. When the lease comes to be renewed, however, the landlord commonly demands the same augmentation of rent as if they had been all made by his own.
p1.zh: 可以认为,土地的租金常常只是房东在改善土地时所列出的股票的合理利润或利息。 毫无疑问,在某些情况下,情况可能部分如此;因为情况很少,可能不止是部分。地主甚至要求为未经改良的土地提供租金,而假定的利息或改善费用带来的利润一般是这种原始租金的附加. 此外,这些改善并非总是由房东的股票,有时是由房客的股票。 但是,当租约被续签时,房东通常要求增加租金,就像所有租金都是他自己做的一样。

p2.original: He sometimes demands rent for what is altogether incapable of human improvements. Kelp is a species of sea-weed, which, when burnt, yields an alkaline salt, useful for making glass, soap, and for several other purposes. It grows in several parts of Great Britain, particularly in Scotland, upon such rocks only as lie within the high-water mark, which are twice every day covered with the sea, and of which the produce, therefore, was never augmented by human industry. The landlord, however, whose estate is bounded by a kelp shore of this kind, demands a rent for it as much as for his corn-fields.
p2.zh: 他有时要求租金,因为完全无法改善人的生活。 海藻是海藻的一种,在烧焦后会产生碱性盐,可用于制造玻璃,肥皂,以及其它几种用途. 它生长在大不列颠的几个地区,特别是在苏格兰,只生长在高水量的岩石上,这些岩石每天有两次被海水覆盖,因此,人类工业从未增加其产品。 然而,地主的地产以这种海藻海岸为界,他要求得到的租金与其玉米田一样多。

p3.original: The sea in the neighbourhood of the islands of Shetland is more than commonly abundant in fish, which makes a great part of the subsistence of their inhabitants. But, in order to profit by the produce of the water, they must have a habitation upon the neighbouring land. The rent of the landlord is in proportion, not to what the farmer can make by the land, but to what he can make both by the land and the water. It is partly paid in sea-fish; and one of the very few instances in which rent makes a part of the price of that commodity, is to be found in that country.
p3.zh: 谢特兰群岛周边海域的鱼类资源普遍丰富,因此是其居民生计的很大一部分. 但是,为了从水的产物中获利,他们必须在邻近的土地上有住所。地主的租金是比例的,不与农民靠土地能挣多少,而是与他靠土地和水都能挣多少.部分由海鱼支付;租金占该商品价格一部分的极少数例子之一,见于该国。

p4.original: The rent of land, therefore, considered as the price paid for the use of the land, is naturally a monopoly price. It is not at all proportioned to what the landlord may have laid out upon the improvement of the land, or to what he can afford to take, but to what the farmer can afford to give.
p4.zh: 因此,土地的租金被认为是土地使用所支付的价格,这自然是一种垄断价格。 它完全不与地主在改善土地时可能规定的内容或他能承受的东西成比例,而是与农民能够负担的东西成比例。

p5.original: Such parts only of the produce of land can commonly be brought to market, of which the ordinary price is sufficient to replace the stock which must be employed in bringing them thither, together with its ordinary profits. If the ordinary price is more than this, the surplus part of it will naturally go to the rent of the land. If it is not more, though the commodity may be brought to market, it can afford no rent to the landlord. Whether the price is, or is not more, depends upon the demand.
p5.zh: 通常,只有这些部分的土地才能进入市场,其中,普通价格足以取代必须用来将它们与普通利润结合起来的股票。 如果普通价格超过这个,剩余部分自然会到土地的租金. 如果不是更多,虽然商品可以上市,但无法负担房东的租金。价格是否更高取决于需求。

p6.original: There are some parts of the produce of land, for which the demand must always be such as to afford a greater price than what is sufficient to bring them to market; and there are others for which it either may or may not be such as to afford this greater price. The former must always afford a rent to the landlord. The latter sometimes may and sometimes may not, according to different circumstances.
p6.zh: 土地的某些生产部分,其需求必须始终达到比将土地带入市场所需的价格更大的程度;还有一些部分,它可能或可能无法达到这种更高的价格。前者必须总是负担房东的租金. 根据不同的情况,后一种情况有时可能有时可能不会。

p7.original: Rent, it is to be observed, therefore, enters into the composition of the price of commodities in a different way from wages and profit. High or low wages and profit are the causes of high or low price; high or low rent is the effect of it. It is because high or low wages and profit must be paid, in order to bring a particular commodity to market, that its price is high or low. But it is because its price is high or low, a great deal more, or very little more, or no more, than what is sufficient to pay those wages and profit, that it affords a high rent, or a low rent, or no rent at all.
p7.zh: 因此,应当注意到,租金是以不同于工资和利润的方式进入商品价格的构成的。高或低工资和利润是高或低价格的原因;高或低租金是其影响. 正是由于高工资或低工资和利润必须支付,才能将某一商品带入市场,所以其价格是高的或低的。然其价高低,多多多少少,或无多多多多,或无多少,足以支付这些工资和利润,所以能负担高租,或低租,或根本无租金.

p8.original: The particular consideration, first, of those parts of the produce of land which always afford some rent; secondly, of those which sometimes may and sometimes may not afford rent; and, thirdly, of the variations which, in the different periods of improvement, naturally take place in the relative value of those two different sorts of rude produce, when compared both with one another and with manufactured commodities, will divide this chapter into three parts.
p8.zh: 首先,特别考虑那些总能负担一定租金的土地的产值;其次,有时可能而且有时可能负担不起租金的土地的产值;第三,在不同的改良时期,自然会因这两种不同粗鲁的产值而有所变化,而两者之间和与制成品相比,将本章分为三个部分。

p9.original: PART I.--Of the Produce of Land which always affords Rent.
p9.zh: 第一部分 - 土地生产公司,它总是提供租金。

p10.original: As men, like all other animals, naturally multiply in proportion to the means of their subsistence, food is always more or less in demand. It can always purchase or command a greater or smaller quantity of labour, and somebody can always be found who is willing to do something in order to obtain it. The quantity of labour, indeed, which it can purchase, is not always equal to what it could maintain, if managed in the most economical manner, on account of the high wages which are sometimes given to labour; but it can always purchase such a quantity of labour as it can maintain, according to the rate at which that sort of labour is commonly maintained in the neighbourhood.
p10.zh: 由于男人和所有其他动物一样,自然地按照生存手段的比例倍增,所以食物总是或多或少的需求. 它总是可以购买或指挥更多或更少的劳动力,总能找到愿意为获得劳动力而做一些事情的人。劳动力的数量,事实上,它可以购买的劳动力数量,如果管理得最经济,则并不总是等同于它能够维持的劳动力数量,因为有时劳动工资很高;但是,它总是能够购买到它能够维持的劳动力数量,这取决于在邻近地区普遍维持这种劳动力的速度。

p11.original: But land, in almost any situation, produces a greater quantity of food than what is sufficient to maintain all the labour necessary for bringing it to market, in the most liberal way in which that labour is ever maintained. The surplus, too, is always more than sufficient to replace the stock which employed that labour, together with its profits. Something, therefore, always remains for a rent to the landlord.
p11.zh: 但是,在几乎任何情况下,土地生产的食物数量都比维持其进入市场所需的一切劳动力数量还要多,这种生产方式最自由。盈余也总是足以取代雇用该劳动力的股票及其利润。 因此,有些东西总是留给房东的租金。

p12.original: The most desert moors in Norway and Scotland produce some sort of pasture for cattle, of which the milk and the increase are always more than sufficient, not only to maintain all the labour necessary for tending them, and to pay the ordinary profit to the farmer or the owner of the herd or flock, but to afford some small rent to the landlord. The rent increases in proportion to the goodness of the pasture. The same extent of ground not only maintains a greater number of cattle, but as they we brought within a smaller compass, less labour becomes requisite to tend them, and to collect their produce. The landlord gains both ways; by the increase of the produce, and by the diminution of the labour which must be maintained out of it.
p12.zh: 挪威和苏格兰最荒漠的荒漠为牛生产某种牧场,其中牛奶和增加量总是足够多,不仅可以维持照料牲畜所需的一切劳动,还可以向农民或畜群或羊群的主人支付一般利润,还可以向地主支付一些小租金.租金按照牧场的好坏比例增加。同样的地层不仅养有较多的牛,而且随着它们被我们带到一个较小的罗盘中,较少的劳动力成为了饲养它们和收集它们的产物的必备条件.地主通过增加产量和减少必须维持的劳动力,从两方面获得收益。

p13.original: The rent of land not only varies with its fertility, whatever be its produce, but with its situation, whatever be its fertility. Land in the neighbourhood of a town gives a greater rent than land equally fertile in a distant part of the country. Though it may cost no more labour to cultivate the one than the other, it must always cost more to bring the produce of the distant land to market. A greater quantity of labour, therefore, must be maintained out of it; and the surplus, from which are drawn both the profit of the farmer and the rent of the landlord, must be diminished. But in remote parts of the country, the rate of profit, as has already been shewn, is generally higher than in the neighbourhood of a large town. A smaller proportion of this diminished surplus, therefore, must belong to the landlord.
p13.zh: 土地的租金不仅随其生育率而变化,无论土地的产量如何,而且随其情况而变化,无论土地的生育率如何。城镇街区的土地比该国遥远地区同样肥沃的土地的租金要高。 虽然种植一种土地的劳动力可能比另一种土地的劳动力少,但将遥远土地的农产品投入市场总要付出更多的代价。 因此,必须维持更多的劳动力;必须减少从中提取的盈余,既要从中提取农民的利润,又要从房东的租金中提取。 但是,在国内的偏远地区,利润率,正如已经表明的那样,一般高于一个大城镇的邻近地区。 因此,减少的盈余中,一小部分必须属于房东。

p14.original: Good roads, canals, and navigable rivers, by diminishing the expense of carriage, put the remote parts of the country more nearly upon a level with those in the neighbourhood of the town. They are upon that account the greatest of all improvements. They encourage the cultivation of the remote, which must always be the most extensive circle of the country. They are advantageous to the town by breaking down the monopoly of the country in its neighbourhood. They are advantageous even to that part of the country. Though they introduce some rival commodities into the old market, they open many new markets to its produce. Monopoly, besides, is a great enemy to good management, which can never be universally established, but in consequence of that free and universal competition which forces every body to have recourse to it for the sake of self defence. It is not more than fifty years ago, that some of the counties in the neighbourhood of London petitioned the parliament against the extension of the turnpike roads into the remoter counties. Those remoter counties, they pretended, from the cheapness of labour, would be able to sell their grass and corn cheaper in the London market than themselves, and would thereby reduce their rents, and ruin their cultivation. Their rents, however, have risen, and their cultivation has been improved since that time.
p14.zh: 良好的道路、运河和可通航的河流,通过减少运输费用,使该国偏远地区与该镇的邻近地区更加接近。在所有改进中,它们都是最大的改进。 它们鼓励种植边远地带,而边远地带必须是该国最广阔的圈子。 它们打破了国家在其邻近地区的垄断地位,从而有利于该镇。 他们甚至对该国的这一地区都有利。 虽然它们将一些竞争对手的商品引入旧市场,但它们为它的农产品开辟了许多新的市场。 此外,垄断是对良好管理的巨大敌人,这种管理永远无法普遍确立,而是由于这种自由和普遍的竞争迫使每个机构为了自卫而诉诸这种管理。不到50年前,伦敦街区的一些郡向议会请愿,反对将转弯路延伸至偏僻的郡. 那些边远的郡,他们假装,从廉价的劳动力,能够在伦敦市场上出售他们的草和玉米比自己便宜,从而降低他们的租金,破坏他们的种植. 然而,他们的租金有所增加,从那时起,他们的种植得到了改善。

p15.original: A corn field of moderate fertility produces a much greater quantity of food for man, than the best pasture of equal extent. Though its cultivation requires much more labour, yet the surplus which remains after replacing the seed and maintaining all that labour, is likewise much greater. If a pound of butcher's meat, therefore, was never supposed to be worth more than a pound of bread, this greater surplus would everywhere be of greater value and constitute a greater fund, both for the profit of the farmer and the rent of the landlord. It seems to have done so universally in the rude beginnings of agriculture.
p15.zh: 中等生育力的玉米田为人类生产的粮食数量比同等程度的最佳牧场多得多。 尽管种植这种作物需要更多的劳动力,但在替换种子和保持全部劳动力之后,剩余的劳动力同样要多得多。 因此,如果屠夫的一斤肉从来不值一斤多面包,那么这种更大的盈余在任何地方都具有更大的价值,并且构成一个更大的基金,既为了农民的利润,也为了地主的租金. 它似乎在粗鲁的农业开始阶段就普遍如此。

p16.original: But the relative values of those two different species of food, bread and butcher's meat, are very different in the different periods of agriculture. In its rude beginnings, the unimproved wilds, which then occupy the far greater part of the country, are all abandoned to cattle. There is more butcher's meat than bread; and bread, therefore, is the food for which there is the greatest competition, and which consequently brings the greatest price. At Buenos Ayres, we are told by Ulloa, four reals, one-and-twenty pence halfpenny sterling, was, forty or fifty years ago, the ordinary price of an ox, chosen from a herd of two or three hundred. He says nothing of the price of bread, probably because he found nothing remarkable about it. An ox there, he says, costs little more than the labour of catching him. But corn can nowhere be raised without a great deal of labour; and in a country which lies upon the river Plate, at that time the direct road from Europe to the silver mines of Potosi, the money-price of labour could be very cheap. It is otherwise when cultivation is extended over the greater part of the country. There is then more bread than butcher's meat. The competition changes its direction, and the price of butcher's meat becomes greater than the price of bread.
p16.zh: 但这两种不同的食物,面包和屠夫肉的相对价值,在不同的农业时期却有很大的不同.在其粗鲁的开端,当时占据了全国大部的未改良的野兽都被遗弃在牛群中.屠夫的肉比面包多;因此,面包是竞争最激烈的食物,因此带来最大的价格。 在布宜诺斯艾利斯艾雷斯,我们被告知 乌尔洛亚,四个真品,一个20便士半便士, 四十或五十年前,牛的普通价格, 从两三百只牛中挑选出来。 他没有说面包的价钱, 可能因为他没有发现任何显著的面包。 他说,一个牛在那里, 花费比抓他的劳累少。 但是,没有大量的劳动力,玉米就无处可提;在一个位于普拉特河畔的国家,当时从欧洲到波托西银矿的直通道路,劳动力的金钱价格可能非常便宜. 否则,种植范围扩大到该国大部分地区。面包比肉肉还多竞争改变方向,屠夫肉的价格变得比面包的价格大.

p17.original: By the extension, besides, of cultivation, the unimproved wilds become insufficient to supply the demand for butcher's meat. A great part of the cultivated lands must be employed in rearing and fattening cattle; of which the price, therefore, must be sufficient to pay, not only the labour necessary for tending them, but the rent which the landlord, and the profit which the farmer, could have drawn from such land employed in tillage. The cattle bred upon the most uncultivated moors, when brought to the same market, are, in proportion to their weight or goodness, sold at the same price as those which are reared upon the most improved land. The proprietors of those moors profit by it, and raise the rent of their land in proportion to the price of their cattle. It is not more than a century ago, that in many parts of the Highlands of Scotland, butcher's meat was as cheap or cheaper than even bread made of oatmeal. The Union opened the market of England to the Highland cattle. Their ordinary price, at present, is about three times greater than at the beginning of the century, and the rents of many Highland estates have been tripled and quadrupled in the same time. In almost every part of Great Britain, a pound of the best butcher's meat is, in the present times, generally worth more than two pounds of the best white bread; and in plentiful years it is sometimes worth three or four pounds.
p17.zh: 由于种植面积的扩大,未改良的野生地变得不足以供应屠夫肉类的需求.相当一部分耕地必须用于饲养和养肥牛;因此,必须有足够的价格来支付,不仅支付照料这些牲畜所需的劳力,而且支付地主本可以从耕地中赚取的租金和农民的利润。 在最未开垦的荒地上饲养的牲畜,如果被带到同一个市场,则按照它们的重量或善良程度,以与在最改良的土地上饲养的牲畜相同的价格出售。 这些荒地的业主从中获利,按照牛的价钱比例提高土地的租金.不到一个世纪前,在苏格兰高地的许多地方,屠夫的肉比燕麦做的面包便宜或便宜.联盟向高地牛开放了英格兰市场. 他们的普通价格,目前比本世纪初高出约三倍,许多高地庄园的租金也同时翻了三倍,翻了两番. 在大不列颠的几乎每一个地区,一磅最好的屠夫肉,在当今的时代,一般价值超过两磅的最好的白面包;在丰满的年份,它有时价值三四磅.

p18.original: It is thus that, in the progress of improvement, the rent and profit of unimproved pasture come to be regulated in some measure by the rent and profit of what is improved, and these again by the rent and profit of corn. Corn is an annual crop; butcher's meat, a crop which requires four or five years to grow. As an acre of land, therefore, will produce a much smaller quantity of the one species of food than of the other, the inferiority of the quantity must be compensated by the superiority of the price. If it was more than compensated, more corn-land would be turned into pasture; and if it was not compensated, part of what was in pasture would be brought back into corn.
p18.zh: 因此,在改进过程中,未改良牧场的租金和利润在某种程度上受到改进牧场的租金和利润的管制,这些也受玉米租金和利润的管制。玉米是一年一度的作物;屠宰的肉类,这种作物需要4到5年才能种植. 因此,作为一亩土地,一个粮食品种的产量将比另一个品种少得多,必须用价格的优越性来补偿这一数量的低劣。 如果得到更多的补偿,更多的玉米地将变成牧场;如果不得到补偿,牧场中的一部分将重新变成玉米。

p19.original: This equality, however, between the rent and profit of grass and those of corn; of the land of which the immediate produce is food for cattle, and of that of which the immediate produce is food for men, must be understood to take place only through the greater part of the improved lands of a great country. In some particular local situations it is quite otherwise, and the rent and profit of grass are much superior to what can be made by corn.
p19.zh: 然而,这种平等必须理解为只有通过一个伟大国家的改良土地的更大部分才能实现,即草的租金和利润与玉米的租金和利润;其中直接产物为牛粮的土地,以及直接产物为男人粮的土地。在某些特定的地方情况中,情况相当不同,草的租金和利润大大高于玉米所能做的。

p20.original: Thus, in the neighbourhood of a great town, the demand for milk, and for forage to horses, frequently contribute, together with the high price of butcher's meat, to raise the value of grass above what may be called its natural proportion to that of corn. This local advantage, it is evident, cannot be communicated to the lands at a distance.
p20.zh: 因此,在一个大城镇的街区,对牛奶和马饲料的需求,加上屠夫肉的高昂价格,往往有助于提高草的价值,使其高于可称为其与玉米的自然比例。 显然,这种当地优势不能远距离传达给土地。

p21.original: Particular circumstances have sometimes rendered some countries so populous, that the whole territory, like the lands in the neighbourhood of a great town, has not been sufficient to produce both the grass and the corn necessary for the subsistence of their inhabitants. Their lands, therefore, have been principally employed in the production of grass, the more bulky commodity, and which cannot be so easily brought from a great distance; and corn, the food of the great body of the people, has been chiefly imported from foreign countries. Holland is at present in this situation; and a considerable part of ancient Italy seems to have been so during the prosperity of the Romans. To feed well, old Cato said, as we are told by Cicero, was the first and most profitable thing in the management of a private estate; to feed tolerably well, the second; and to feed ill, the third. To plough, he ranked only in the fourth place of profit and advantage. Tillage, indeed, in that part of ancient Italy which lay in the neighbour hood of Rome, must have been very much discouraged by the distributions of corn which were frequently made to the people, either gratuitously, or at a very low price. This corn was brought from the conquered provinces, of which several, instead of taxes, were obliged to furnish a tenth part of their produce at a stated price, about sixpence a-peck, to the republic. The low price at which this corn was distributed to the people, must necessarily have sunk the price of what could be brought to the Roman market from Latium, or the ancient territory of Rome, and must have discouraged its cultivation in that country.
p21.zh: 特殊情况有时使一些国家人口众多,以致整个领土,如一个大城镇附近的土地,不足以生产其居民生存所必需的草和玉米。 因此,他们的土地主要用于生产草,即较大宗的商品,而从很远的地方不能轻易地运来;玉米,即人民大身体的粮食,主要从外国进口。 荷兰目前处于这种情况;古意大利相当一部分似乎在罗马人繁荣时期就如此. 老卡托说,为了养活好,正如西塞罗告诉我们的那样,这是管理私人庄园的第一个,也是最有利可图的东西;为了养活好,第二个;为了养活病人,第三个。至犁头,他只排名利润和优势的第4位. 事实上,在古意大利这个位于罗马邻国的地盘上的那部分,玉米的分发必须非常令人沮丧,因为玉米的分发常常是毫无理由地或以非常低的价格向人民生产的。 这种玉米是从被征服的省份运来的,其中几个省不得不以规定的价格向共和国提供其生产的十分之一,即大约六便士一斤。将这种玉米分给人民的低价,必然使从拉提姆或古老的罗马领地可以带给罗马市场的东西的价格下沉,一定阻止了它在该国的种植.

p22.original: In an open country, too, of which the principal produce is corn, a well-inclosed piece of grass will frequently rent higher than any corn field in its neighbourhood. It is convenient for the maintenance of the cattle employed in the cultivation of the corn; and its high rent is, in this case, not so properly paid from the value of its own produce, as from that of the corn lands which are cultivated by means of it. It is likely to fall, if ever the neighbouring lands are completely inclosed. The present high rent of inclosed land in Scotland seems owing to the scarcity of inclosure, and will probably last no longer than that scarcity. The advantage of inclosure is greater for pasture than for corn. It saves the labour of guarding the cattle, which feed better, too, when they are not liable to be disturbed by their keeper or his dog.
p22.zh: 在一个开放的国家,主要产品是玉米,一个封闭的草地的租金往往比其邻近地区任何玉米田都要高。用于种植玉米的牲畜的维修是方便的;在这种情况下,其高租金不是从自己的产品的价值中适当支付,而是从通过玉米种植的玉米地的价值中支付。 如果邻近土地完全封闭,它很可能会倒塌。 目前苏格兰的封闭土地租金很高,似乎是因为缺乏封闭,而且可能不会持续到这种匮乏。 对牧场而言,封锁的好处大于玉米。 它可以节省守护牛的劳动,当牛不受饲养者或他的狗的干扰时,牛的饲养也更好.

p23.original: But where there is no local advantage of this kind, the rent and profit of corn, or whatever else is the common vegetable food of the people, must naturally regulate upon the land which is fit for producing it, the rent and profit of pasture.
p23.zh: 但是,如果当地没有这种优势,玉米的租金和利润,或者其他什么是人民的共同蔬菜食品,就必须自然地调节适合生产这种蔬菜的土地,牧场的租金和利润.

p24.original: The use of the artificial grasses, of turnips, carrots, cabbages, and the other expedients which have been fallen upon to make an equal quantity of land feed a greater number of cattle than when in natural grass, should somewhat reduce, it might be expected, the superiority which, in an improved country, the price of butcher's meat naturally has over that of bread. It seems accordingly to have done so; and there is some reason for believing that, at least in the London market, the price of butcher's meat, in proportion to the price of bread, is a good deal lower in the present times than it was in the beginning of the last century.
p24.zh: 利用人工草、萝卜、胡萝卜、小白菜以及其他使同样数量的土地喂养牛的权宜之计,比自然草丛中时要多一些,这应该有所降低,可以预期,在一个改良的国家,屠宰肉的价格自然高于面包的价格。 它似乎也相应地这样做了;并且有某种理由相信,至少在伦敦市场里,按照面包价格的比例,屠夫肉的价格在当今时代比上个世纪初要低很多.

p25.original: In the Appendix to the life of Prince Henry, Doctor Birch has given us an account of the prices of butcher's meat as commonly paid by that prince. It is there said, that the four quarters of an ox, weighing six hundred pounds, usually cost him nine pounds ten shillings, or thereabouts; that is thirty-one shillings and eight-pence per hundred pounds weight. Prince Henry died on the 6th of November 1612, in the nineteenth year of his age.
p25.zh: 在亨利王子生平的附录中,伯奇医生向我们介绍了这位王子通常支付的屠夫肉的价格. 据说,一头牛的4/4,重600磅,通常要花9磅10先令,或者大约在那里;即每百磅重31先令和8便士.亨利王子于1612年11月6日去世,享年19岁.

p26.original: In March 1764, there was a parliamentary inquiry into the causes of the high price of provisions at that time. It was then, among other proof to the same purpose, given in evidence by a Virginia merchant, that in March 1763, he had victualled his ships for twentyfour or twenty-five shillings the hundred weight of beef, which he considered as the ordinary price; whereas, in that dear year, he had paid twenty-seven shillings for the same weight and sort. This high price in 1764 is, however, four shillings and eight-pence cheaper than the ordinary price paid by Prince Henry; and it is the best beef only, it must be observed, which is fit to be salted for those distant voyages.
p26.zh: 1764年3月,议会对当时规定价格高的原因进行了调查.之后,作为同样目的的其他证据之一,一位弗吉尼亚商人在证据中证明,1763年3月,他以24或25先令的价格将他的舰只的牛肉的百重视为普通价格;而在那个亲爱的年份,他为同样重量和种类支付了27先令. 然而,1764年的这种高价比亨利王子所付的普通价格便宜4先令和8便士;它是唯一最好的牛肉,必须被观察到,这适合于这些远航.

p27.original: The price paid by Prince Henry amounts to 3d. 4/5ths per pound weight of the whole carcase, coarse and choice pieces taken together; and at that rate the choice pieces could not have been sold by retail for less than 4½d. or 5d. the pound.
p27.zh: 亨利王子支付的价格为3d.整个车厢、粗皮和选择品的重量为每磅4/5;按这一速度,选择品不可能由零售商出售,售价不到41%/天或5天。

p28.original: In the parliamentary inquiry in 1764, the witnesses stated the price of the choice pieces of the best beef to be to the consumer 4d. and 4½d. the pound; and the coarse pieces in general to be from seven farthings to 2½d. and 2¾d.; and this, they said, was in general one halfpenny dearer than the same sort of pieces had usually been sold in the month of March. But even this high price is still a good deal cheaper than what we can well suppose the ordinary retail price to have been in the time of Prince Henry.
p28.zh: 在1764年的议会质询中,目击者表示最佳牛肉的选择片的价格是给消费者4d和41⁄2d的磅;粗细的片段一般从7个远到21⁄2和23⁄4d;他们说,这一般比通常在3月份出售的同类片段多一半。 但即使是这种高价,还是比我们推测的普通零售价格在亨利王子时代的价格要便宜的好.

p29.original: During the first twelve years of the last century, the average price of the best wheat at the Windsor market was £ 1:18:3½d. the quarter of nine Winchester bushels.
p29.zh: 在上个世纪的前十二年间,温莎市场最好的小麦的平均价格是1:118:31⁄2英镑. 温彻斯特的9个灌木丛的四分之一.

p30.original: But in the twelve years preceding 1764 including that year, the average price of the same measure of the best wheat at the same market was £ 2:1:9½d.
p30.zh: 但在1764年之前的12年中,包括当年,同一市场同样衡量最佳小麦的平均价格为2:1:91⁄2d英镑.

p31.original: In the first twelve years of the last century, therefore, wheat appears to have been a good deal cheaper, and butcher's meat a good deal dearer, than in the twelve years preceding 1764, including that year.
p31.zh: 因此,在上个世纪的前十二年,小麦似乎比1764年之前的十二年,包括当年,便宜得多,屠夫的肉也比那一年更珍贵.

p32.original: In all great countries, the greater part of the cultivated lands are employed in producing either food for men or food for cattle. The rent and profit of these regulate the rent and profit of all other cultivated land. If any particular produce afforded less, the land would soon be turned into corn or pasture; and if any afforded more, some part of the lands in corn or pasture would soon be turned to that produce.
p32.zh: 在所有伟大的国家,大部分耕地都用于生产男子食品或牛粮。 这些土地的租金和利润调节着所有其他耕地的租金和利润。 如果获得的农产品少,土地很快会变成玉米或牧场;如果获得更多的土地,玉米或牧场的某些土地很快会变成这种作物。

p33.original: Those productions, indeed, which require either a greater original expense of improvement, or a greater annual expense of cultivation in order to fit the land for them, appear commonly to afford, the one a greater rent, the other a greater profit, than corn or pasture. This superiority, however, will seldom be found to amount to more than a reasonable interest or compensation for this superior expense.
p33.zh: 实际上,这些生产要么需要更多的原始改良费用,要么需要更多的年度种植费用,以便适合他们的土地,这些生产似乎通常比玉米或牧场更能负担更大的租金,而另一个则比玉米或牧场更能获利。 然而,这种优越性很少被认为超过合理利息或补偿这一高额费用。

p34.original: In a hop garden, a fruit garden, a kitchen garden, both the rent of the landlord, and the profit of the farmer, are generally greater than in acorn or grass field. But to bring the ground into this condition requires more expense. Hence a greater rent becomes due to the landlord. It requires, too, a more attentive and skilful management. Hence a greater profit becomes due to the farmer. The crop, too, at least in the hop and fruit garden, is more precarious. Its price, therefore, besides compensating all occasional losses, must afford something like the profit of insurance. The circumstances of gardeners, generally mean, and always moderate, may satisfy us that their great ingenuity is not commonly over-recompensed. Their delightful art is practised by so many rich people for amusement, that little advantage is to be made by those who practise it for profit; because the persons who should naturally be their best customers, supply themselves with all their most precious productions.
p34.zh: 在跳楼花园,果园,厨房花园,既收房主的租金,又收农户的利润,一般都比橡树或草场的要大. 但是,要将地面带入这一状况,需要花费更多的费用。 因此,房东应得的租金要高一些。还需要更认真和更熟练的管理。 因此,农民应获得更大的利润。作物,至少是在跳跃和果园里,也更加不稳定. 因此,其价格除了补偿所有偶发损失外,还必须支付保险的利润。园丁的情况,一般地说,而且总是温和的,可能令我们确信,他们伟大的才智,通常不会得到过度补偿.如此众多的富人为了娱乐而表演了他们的令人愉快的艺术,那些为了盈利而进行这种艺术的人却没有多大好处;因为那些自然应该成为他们最佳顾客的人,提供他们所有最珍贵的作品。

p35.original: The advantage which the landlord derives from such improvements, seems at no time to have been greater than what was sufficient to compensate the original expense of making them. In the ancient husbandry, after the vineyard, a well-watered kitchen garden seems to have been the part of the farm which was supposed to yield the most valuable produce. But Democritus, who wrote upon husbandry about two thousand years ago, and who was regarded by the ancients as one of the fathers of the art, thought they did not act wisely who inclosed a kitchen garden. The profit, he said, would not compensate the expense of a stone-wall: and bricks (he meant, I suppose, bricks baked in the sun) mouldered with the rain and the winter-storm, and required continual repairs. Columella, who reports this judgment of Democritus, does not controvert it, but proposes a very frugal method of inclosing with a hedge of brambles and briars, which he says he had found by experience to be both a lasting and an impenetrable fence; but which, it seems, was not commonly known in the time of Democritus. Palladius adopts the opinion of Columella, which had before been recommended by Varro. In the judgment of those ancient improvers, the produce of a kitchen garden had, it seems, been little more than sufficient to pay the extraordinary culture and the expense of watering; for in countries so near the sun, it was thought proper, in those times as in the present, to have the command of a stream of water, which could be conducted to every bed in the garden. Through the greater part of Europe, a kitchen garden is not at present supposed to deserve a better inclosure than mat recommended by Columella. In Great Britain, and some other northern countries, the finer fruits cannot be brought to perfection but by the assistance of a wall. Their price, therefore, in such countries, must be sufficient to pay the expense of building and maintaining what they cannot be had without. The fruit-wall frequently surrounds the kitchen garden, which thus enjoys the benefit of an inclosure which its own produce could seldom pay for.
p35.zh: 房东从这种改善中获得的好处似乎从未超过足以补偿原始费用的数额。 在古代的畜牧业中,葡萄园之后,一个水分良好的厨房花园似乎是农场的一部分,它本应生产最有价值的农产品。 但德莫克里图斯大约在两千年前写了一篇关于畜牧业的文章,被古代人视为艺术之父之一,认为他们不明智地行动,谁封闭了厨房花园. 他说,利润不会补偿石墙的费用:砖块(他的意思是,在阳光下烤成的砖块)用雨水和冬季暴风雨铸造,需要不断修理。科卢梅拉报告了德莫克里图斯的这一判断,并没有反悔,而是提出了一种非常节俭的方法,用布拉姆布和布拉尔的树篱来关闭,他说,根据经验他发现这既是一个持久又坚不可摧的栅栏;但是,这似乎在德莫克里图斯时代并不为人所熟知.帕拉迪乌斯采纳了科卢梅拉的意见,而科卢梅拉的意见此前是瓦罗推荐的. 根据这些古代改良者们的判断,厨房花园的产物,似乎还不足以支付非凡的文化和水费;因为在离太阳如此近的国家,人们觉得在像现在这样的时候,有一条水流的指挥权是适当的,可以把水流带到花园的每一张床. 通过欧洲大部分地区,一个厨房花园目前不应该比科卢梅拉推荐的垫子更值得封闭. 在大不列颠和一些其他北方国家,精细的水果不能完美地得到,只能靠墙壁的帮助。 因此,在这些国家,其价格必须足以支付建造和维持它们无法拥有的东西的费用。果墙经常围在厨房花园周围,因此,厨房花园享有自己产品很少能够支付的封闭性好处。

p36.original: That the vineyard, when properly planted and brought to perfection, was the most valuable part of the farm, seems to have been an undoubted maxim in the ancient agriculture, as it is in the modern, through all the wine countries. But whether it was advantageous to plant a new vineyard, was a matter of dispute among the ancient Italian husbandmen, as we learn from Columella. He decides, like a true lover of all curious cultivation, in favour of the vineyard; and endeavours to shew, by a comparison of the profit and expense, that it was a most advantageous improvement. Such comparisons, however, between the profit and expense of new projects are commonly very fallacious; and in nothing more so than in agriculture. Had the gain actually made by such plantations been commonly as great as he imagined it might have been, there could have been no dispute about it. The same point is frequently at this day a matter of controversy in the wine countries. Their writers on agriculture, indeed, the lovers and promoters of high cultivation, seem generally disposed to decide with Columella in favour of the vineyard. In France, the anxiety of the proprietors of the old vineyards to prevent the planting of any new ones, seems to favour their opinion, and to indicate a consciousness in those who must have the experience, that this species of cultivation is at present in that country more profitable than any other. It seems, at the same time, however, to indicate another opinion, that this superior profit can last no longer than the laws which at present restrain the free cultivation of the vine. In 1731, they obtained an order of council, prohibiting both the planting of new vineyards, and the renewal of these old ones, of which the cultivation had been interrupted for two years, without a particular permission from the king, to be granted only in consequence of an information from the intendant of the province, certifying that he had examined the land, and that it was incapable of any other culture. The pretence of this order was the scarcity of corn and pasture, and the superabundance of wine. But had this superabundance been real, it would, without any order of council, have effectually prevented the plantation of new vineyards, by reducing the profits of this species of cultivation below their natural proportion to those of corn and pasture. With regard to the supposed scarcity of corn occasioned by the multiplication of vineyards, corn is nowhere in France more carefully cultivated than in the wine provinces, where the land is fit for producing it: as in Burgundy, Guienne, and the Upper Languedoc. The numerous hands employed in the one species of cultivation necessarily encourage the other, by affording a ready market for its produce. To diminish the number of those who are capable of paying it, is surely a most unpromising expedient for encouraging the cultivation of corn. It is like the policy which would promote agriculture, by discouraging manufactures.
p36.zh: 葡萄园在种植和完美时 是农场中最有价值的部分 似乎是古代农业中无可置疑的格言 就像现代一样 遍及所有葡萄酒国 但种植新葡萄园是否有利,是古代意大利夫君之间的争议,就像我们从科卢梅拉那里学到的. 他像一个所有好奇种植的真正爱好者一样,决定赞成葡萄园;并且努力通过利润和开支的比较来示众,认为这是一个最有利的改进. 然而,在新项目的利润和开支之间作这种比较,通常非常荒谬;在农业方面,情况更是这样。 如果这种种植园的实际收益与他想象的一样大,就不会有争议。 同样的一点是,在今天,酒国经常发生争议。 他们关于农业的作家,实际上,是高种植的爱好者和提倡者,似乎一般都愿意与科卢梅拉一起决定赞成葡萄园. 在法国,旧葡萄园的主人们对于阻止任何新葡萄园的种植感到焦虑,似乎倾向于他们的意见,并且表明那些必须有这种经验的人有一种意识,即这种种植品种目前在该国比任何其他品种都更有利可图. 然而,与此同时,似乎也表示了另一种看法,即这种优越的利润不能超过目前限制自由种植藤类作物的法律。1731年,他们获得了议会的命令,既禁止种植新的葡萄园,又禁止这些旧葡萄园的续展,其中种植中断了两年,没有国王的特别许可,只有在该省的意向者提供的消息证明他已经检查过这片土地,并且证明它没有任何其他文化能力的情况下,才准许种植. 这一命令的借口是玉米和牧场的稀缺,以及酒的超丰度. 但是,如果这种超丰盛是真实的,那么,如果没有任何议会的命令,它实际上就阻止了新葡萄园的种植,将这种种植的利润减少到低于玉米和牧场的自然比例。 关于葡萄园繁多导致的所谓玉米稀缺,法国最谨慎的种植玉米的地方是葡萄酒省份,这里的土地适合生产玉米:如勃艮第,吉安,上兰圭多克.一种栽培品种中大量使用的手势必然会鼓励另一种品种,为其产品提供现成的市场。减少有能力支付这种费用的人数,无疑是鼓励种植玉米的最不切实际的时机。 它就像通过阻止制成品而促进农业的政策。

p37.original: The rent and profit of those productions, therefore, which require either a greater original expense of improvement in order to fit the land for them, or a greater annual expense of cultivation, though often much superior to those of corn and pasture, yet when they do no more than compensate such extraordinary expense, are in reality regulated by the rent and profit of those common crops.
p37.zh: 因此,这些生产的租金和利润,要么需要更多的原始改良费,以适合他们的土地,要么需要更多的年度种植费,尽管往往比玉米和牧场的种植费高得多,然而,当它们只补偿这种特殊开支时,实际上却受到这些共同作物的租金和利润的制约。

p38.original: It sometimes happens, indeed, that the quantity of land which can be fitted for some particular produce, is too small to supply the effectual demand. The whole produce can be disposed of to those who are willing to give somewhat more than what is sufficient to pay the whole rent, wages, and profit, necessary for raising and bringing it to market, according to their natural rates, or according to the rates at which they are paid in the greater part of other cultivated land. The surplus part of the price which remains after defraying the whole expense of improvement and cultivation, may commonly, in this case, and in this case only, bear no regular proportion to the like surplus in corn or pasture, but may exceed it in almost any degree; and the greater part of this excess naturally goes to the rent of the landlord.
p38.zh: 有时,确实发生的情况是,可用于某些特定产品的土地数量太小,无法满足实际需求。整个农产品可以交给那些愿意给予的,比支付全部租金、工资和利润还多的人,这些收入是按其自然利率,或者根据在其他大部分耕地的支付率来筹集和上市所必需的。 在支付改良和种植的全部费用之后,剩余部分的价格通常可能在此情况下,而且仅在此情况下,与玉米或牧场的类似剩余部分没有固定比例,但几乎可以超过任何程度;而这一剩余部分中的大部分自然属于房东的租金。

p39.original: The usual and natural proportion, for example, between the rent and profit of wine, and those of corn and pasture, must be understood to take place only with regard to those vineyards which produce nothing but good common wine, such as can be raised almost anywhere, upon any light, gravelly, or sandy soil, and which has nothing to recommend it but its strength and wholesomeness. It is with such vineyards only, that the common land of the country can be brought into competition; for with those of a peculiar quality it is evident that it cannot.
p39.zh: 例如,葡萄酒的租金和利润与玉米和牧场的租金和利润之间的通常比例和自然比例,必须理解为只针对那些只生产好普通葡萄酒的葡萄园,如几乎任何地方都能在任何光线、砾石或沙质土壤上提拔的葡萄园,除了其强度和舒适性外,没有什么可推荐的。只有在这种葡萄园中,才能使国家的共同土地发生竞争;因为与具有特殊质量的土地竞争,显然不能。

p40.original: The vine is more affected by the difference of soils than any other fruit-tree. From some it derives a flavour which no culture or management can equal, it is supposed, upon any other. This flavour, real or imaginary, is sometimes peculiar to the produce of a few vineyards; sometimes it extends through the greater part of a small district, and sometimes through a considerable part of a large province. The whole quantity of such wines that is brought to market falls short of the effectual demand, or the demand of those who would be willing to pay the whole rent, profit, and wages, necessary for preparing and bringing them thither, according to the ordinary rate, or according to the rate at which they are paid in common vineyards. The whole quantity, therefore, can be disposed of to those who are willing to pay more, which necessarily raises their price above that of common wine. The difference is greater or less, according as the fashionableness and scarcity of the wine render the competition of the buyers more or less eager. Whatever it be, the greater part of it goes to the rent of the landlord. For though such vineyards are in general more carefully cultivated than most others, the high price of the wine seems to be, not so much the effect, as the cause of this careful cultivation. In so valuable a produce, the loss occasioned by negligence is so great, as to force even the most careless to attention. A small part of this high price, therefore, is sufficient to pay the wages of the extraordinary labour bestowed upon their cultivation, and the profits of the extraordinary stock which puts that labour into motion.
p40.zh: 与任何其他果树相比,藤叶受土壤差异的影响更大. 从某些人那里得到一种风味,任何文化或管理都不能平等,这种风味在任何其他人身上都是理所当然的。 这种味味,真实的或想象的,有时是少数葡萄园的产物所特有的;有时它延伸至小区的较大部分,有时则延伸至大省的相当部分.上市的这类葡萄酒的总量低于实际需求,或低于愿意支付全部租金、利润和工资的人的需求,而这些都是按普通价格或按在普通葡萄园中支付的价格准备和带回这些葡萄酒所必需的。 因此,全部数量可以处置给那些愿意付出更多钱的人,这必然会使其价格高于普通葡萄酒.差别很大或更少,因为葡萄酒的时髦和稀缺使得买家的竞争或多或少地急于进行. 不管是什么,它的大部分都归房东的租金. 虽然这种葡萄园一般比大多数葡萄园的栽培更为谨慎,但葡萄酒的高价似乎不是如此,而是这种精心栽培的原因. 在如此珍贵的产物中,由于疏忽造成的损失是如此之大,以至于甚至迫使最不小心的注意. 因此,这种高价的一小部分足以支付种植这些农户所得的超寻常劳力的工资,以及使这种劳力开始活动的超常牲畜的利润。

p41.original: The sugar colonies possessed by the European nations in the West Indies may be compared to those precious vineyards. Their whole produce falls short of the effectual demand of Europe, and can be disposed of to those who are willing to give more than what is sufficient to pay the whole rent, profit, and wages, necessary for preparing and bringing it to market, according to the rate at which they are commonly paid by any other produce. In Cochin China, the finest white sugar generally sells for three piastres the quintal, about thirteen shillings and sixpence of our money, as we are told by Mr Poivre {Voyages d'un Philosophe.}, a very careful observer of the agriculture of that country. What is there called the quintal, weighs from a hundred and fifty to two hundred Paris pounds, or a hundred and seventy-five Paris pounds at a medium, which reduces the price of the hundred weight English to about eight shillings sterling; not a fourth part of what is commonly paid for the brown or muscovada sugars imported from our colonies, and not a sixth part of what is paid for the finest white sugar. The greater part of the cultivated lands in Cochin China are employed in producing corn and rice, the food of the great body of the people. The respective prices of corn, rice, and sugar, are there probably in the natural proportion, or in that which naturally takes place in the different crops of the greater part of cultivated land, and which recompenses the landlord and farmer, as nearly as can be computed, according to what is usually the original expense of improvement, and the annual expense of cultivation. But in our sugar colonies, the price of sugar bears no such proportion to that of the produce of a rice or corn field either in Europe or America. It is commonly said that a sugar planter expects that the rum and the molasses should defray the whole expense of his cultivation, and that his sugar should be all clear profit. If this be true, for I pretend not to affirm it, it is as if a corn farmer expected to defray the expense of his cultivation with the chaff and the straw, and that the grain should be all clear profit. We see frequently societies of merchants in London, and other trading towns, purchase waste lands in our sugar colonies, which they expect to improve and cultivate with profit, by means of factors and agents, notwithstanding the great distance and the uncertain returns, from the defective administration of justice in those countries. Nobody will attempt to improve and cultivate in the same manner the most fertile lands of Scotland, Ireland, or the corn provinces of North America, though, from the more exact administration of justice in these countries, more regular returns might be expected.
p41.zh: 欧洲国家在西印度群岛拥有的糖类殖民地可以与这些珍贵的葡萄园相比.其全部产品都低于欧洲的实际需求,可以按照任何其他产品通常支付的价格,向愿意付出超出支付全部租金、利润和工资所需数额的人出售,以准备和将其投入市场。 在科钦中国,最好的白糖一般卖掉3个圆柱,大约13先令和6便士,正如Poivre {Voyages d'un Philosophe先生所说的,他是该国农业的非常仔细的观察者。所谓的“ ⁇ ”从一百五十磅到二百磅,或者说一百七十五磅的巴黎磅在中间,这把百磅的英语价格降低到八先令左右;而不是通常从我们殖民地进口的棕色或木斯卡瓦达糖的四分之一,而不是最好的白糖的六分之一。 中国科钦的大部分耕地都用于生产玉米和水稻,这是人民伟大身体的粮食。玉米、水稻和糖的价格可能与自然成比例,或自然存在于耕地大部的不同作物中,对地主和农民给予报酬,几乎可以按照通常的改良成本和每年的种植成本计算。 但在我们的糖聚居区,糖的价格与欧洲或美洲的稻谷或玉米田的产量没有这么大的比例。 一般说来,一个制糖厂期望朗姆酒和糖浆能支付他种植的全部费用,他的制糖应该全部是明显的利润. 如果这是真的,因为我假装不肯定,这就像一个玉米农希望用玉米和稻草来支付他的种植费用,而且谷物应该全部是明显的利润。 我们经常看到伦敦的商人协会和其他贸易城镇在我们糖地集聚地购买荒地,他们期望通过各种因素和代理人来改善和以利润耕种这些荒地,尽管这些国家的司法存在缺陷,而且收益不确定。 没有人会试图以同样的方式改善和耕种苏格兰、爱尔兰或北美玉米省最肥沃的土地,不过,从这些国家更精确的司法情况来看,预期会有更多的定期回返。

p42.original: In Virginia and Maryland, the cultivation of tobacco is preferred, as most profitable, to that of corn. Tobacco might be cultivated with advantage through the greater part of Europe; but, in almost every part of Europe, it has become a principal subject of taxation; and to collect a tax from every different farm in the country where this plant might happen to be cultivated, would be more difficult, it has been supposed, than to levy one upon its importation at the custom-house. The cultivation of tobacco has, upon this account, been most absurdly prohibited through the greater part of Europe, which necessarily gives a sort of monopoly to the countries where it is allowed; and as Virginia and Maryland produce the greatest quantity of it, they share largely, though with some competitors, in the advantage of this monopoly. The cultivation of tobacco, however, seems not to be so advantageous as that of sugar. I have never even heard of any tobacco plantation that was improved and cultivated by the capital of merchants who resided in Great Britain; and our tobacco colonies send us home no such wealthy planters as we see frequently arrive from our sugar islands. Though, from the preference given in those colonies to the cultivation of tobacco above that of corn, it would appear that the effectual demand of Europe for tobacco is not completely supplied, it probably is more nearly so than that for sugar; and though the present price of tobacco is probably more than sufficient to pay the whole rent, wages, and profit, necessary for preparing and bringing it to market, according to the rate at which they are commonly paid in corn land, it must not be so much more as the present price of sugar. Our tobacco planters, accordingly, have shewn the same fear of the superabundance of tobacco, which the proprietors of the old vineyards in France have of the superabundance of wine. By act of assembly, they have restrained its cultivation to six thousand plants, supposed to yield a thousand weight of tobacco, for every negro between sixteen and sixty years of age. Such a negro, over and above this quantity of tobacco, can manage, they reckon, four acres of Indian corn. To prevent the market from being overstocked, too, they have sometimes, in plentiful years, we are told by Dr Douglas {Douglas's Summary, vol. ii. p. 379, 373.} (I suspect he has been ill informed), burnt a certain quantity of tobacco for every negro, in the same manner as the Dutch are said to do of spices. If such violent methods are necessary to keep up the present price of tobacco, the superior advantage of its culture over that of corn, if it still has any, will not probably be of long continuance.
p42.zh: 在弗吉尼亚州和马里兰州,种植烟草比种植玉米更受青睐,因为种植最有利可图。烟草可通过欧洲大部分地区有利地种植;但是,在欧洲几乎每一个地区,烟草都已成为主要征税对象;从可能种植烟草的所在国的每一个不同农场征税,比在海关进口烟草要困难得多。 因此,通过欧洲大部分地区最荒谬地禁止了烟草的种植,这必然会给允许烟草种植的国家带来某种垄断;由于弗吉尼亚州和马里兰州生产的烟草数量最多,它们基本上分享,尽管它们与一些竞争者分享了这种垄断的好处。 然而,烟草种植似乎不如糖种植那么有利。 我甚至从未听说过任何烟草种植园是由居住在大不列颠的商人的首都改良和种植的;我们的烟草殖民地使我们没有像我们经常看到的那样从我们的糖岛运来的富裕的种植者。 虽然从这些殖民地对烟草种植的偏好到玉米以上,欧洲对烟草的实际需求似乎没有完全供应,但可能比对糖的需求更接近于供应;而且尽管目前的烟草价格可能足以支付全部租金、工资和利润,而这是准备和将其带入市场所必需的,但根据玉米地通常支付的价格,它决不能比目前糖的价格高得多。 因此,我们的烟草种植者对烟草的超丰度也抱有同样的恐惧,法国老葡萄园的所有人对葡萄酒的超丰度也抱有同样的恐惧。 他们通过组装行为,限制种植六千株植物,每只16至60岁的黑人,应该能产生一千重的烟草。 这种黑人,除了这些烟草之外, 他们估计可以管理4英亩的印度玉米。 为了防止市场也过度囤积,他们有时在繁忙的岁月里,被Douglas博士的{Douglas's Cruision, vol. ii. p.379,373}(我怀疑他不知道),用荷兰人所说的调味品的方式,为每个黑人焚烧了一定数量的烟草。 如果这种暴力手段是维持烟草目前价格所必要的,那么,烟草文化比玉米文化的优越优势,如果还有的话,很可能不会长久持续下去。

p43.original: It is in this manner that the rent of the cultivated land, of which the produce is human food, regulates the rent of the greater part of other cultivated land. No particular produce can long afford less, because the land would immediately be turned to another use; and if any particular produce commonly affords more, it is because the quantity of land which can be fitted for it is too small to supply the effectual demand.
p43.zh: 正是通过这种方式,将耕地的租金,其中产物为人粮的,对其他大部分耕地的租金进行管理.任何特定产品都无法长期负担较少的费用,因为土地将立即转为另一种用途;如果任何特定产品通常能负担更多的费用,那是因为能够配给土地的土地数量太少,无法满足实际需求。

p44.original: In Europe, corn is the principal produce of land, which serves immediately for human food. Except in particular situations, therefore, the rent of corn land regulates in Europe that of all other cultivated land. Britain need envy neither the vineyards of France, nor the olive plantations of Italy. Except in particular situations, the value of these is regulated by that of corn, in which the fertility of Britain is not much inferior to that of either of those two countries.
p44.zh: 在欧洲,玉米是土地的主要产物,它立即为人类提供食物。 因此,除特殊情况外,在欧洲,玉米土地的租金对所有其他耕地的租金作了规定。英国既不需要羡慕法国的葡萄园,也不需要羡慕意大利的橄榄种植园. 除特殊情况外,玉米的价值由玉米来调节,在玉米中,英国的生育率并不比这两个国家中任何一个低很多。

p45.original: If, in any country, the common and favourite vegetable food of the people should be drawn from a plant of which the most common land, with the same, or nearly the same culture, produced a much greater quantity than the most fertile does of corn; the rent of the landlord, or the surplus quantity of food which would remain to him, after paying the labour, and replacing the stock of the farmer, together with its ordinary profits, would necessarily be much greater. Whatever was the rate at which labour was commonly maintained in that country, this greater surplus could always maintain a greater quantity of it, and, consequently, enable the landlord to purchase or command a greater quantity of it. The real value of his rent, his real power and authority, his command of the necessaries and conveniencies of life with which the labour of other people could supply him, would necessarily be much greater.
p45.zh: 如果在任何国家,人们的共同和最喜爱的蔬菜食品应该来自一种植物,其中最常见的土地,拥有同样的或几乎相同的文化,生产的数量比最肥沃的玉米多得多;地主的租金,或剩余的粮食,在支付劳动后留给他,并且用普通利润取代农民的库存,必然要大得多。 无论在该国普遍维持多少劳动力,这种较大的盈余总是可以维持更多的劳动力,从而使房东能够购买或支配更多的劳动力。 他的租金的真正价值、他的真正权力和权威、他对生活必需品的指挥权以及其他人的劳动能够给他提供的生活便利,必然会大得多。

p46.original: A rice field produces a much greater quantity of food than the most fertile corn field. Two crops in the year, from thirty to sixty bushels each, are said to be the ordinary produce of an acre. Though its cultivation, therefore, requires more labour, a much greater surplus remains after maintaining all that labour. In those rice countries, therefore, where rice is the common and favourite vegetable food of the people, and where the cultivators are chiefly maintained with it, a greater share of this greater surplus should belong to the landlord than in corn countries. In Carolina, where the planters, as in other British colonies, are generally both farmers and landlords, and where rent, consequently, is confounded with profit, the cultivation of rice is found to be more profitable than that of corn, though their fields produce only one crop in the year, and though, from the prevalence of the customs of Europe, rice is not there the common and favourite vegetable food of the people.
p46.zh: 稻田的粮食产量远大于最肥沃的玉米田。一年有两种作物,每株为30至60灌木,据说是一亩的普通产物. 因此,虽然种植需要更多的劳动力,但在保持所有这些劳动力之后,仍有更多的剩余资源。 因此,在稻米国家,稻米是人民的共同和最喜爱的蔬菜食品,种植者主要拥有这种蔬菜,因此,在这种更大的盈余中,更多的份额应属于地主,而不是玉米国。 在卡罗来纳州,种植者与其他英国殖民地一样,一般都是农民和地主,因此租金与利润相抵,因此发现种植水稻比种植玉米更有利可图,尽管他们的田地当年只生产一种作物,尽管从欧洲风俗的盛行来看,水稻并不存在人民所喜爱的常见蔬菜食品.

p47.original: A good rice field is a bog at all seasons, and at one season a bog covered with water. It is unfit either for corn, or pasture, or vineyard, or, indeed, for any other vegetable produce that is very useful to men; and the lands which are fit for those purposes are not fit for rice. Even in the rice countries, therefore, the rent of rice lands cannot regulate the rent of the other cuitivated land which can never be turned to that produce.
p47.zh: 一个好的稻田是各个季节的沼泽,一个季节的沼泽被水覆盖. 它既不适合玉米、牧场、葡萄园,也不适合任何其他对男人非常有用的蔬菜产品;适合这些用途的土地不适合稻米。 因此,即使在稻谷国,稻田的租金也无法管制其他自来水土地的租金,这些土地永远不能转向这种生产。

p48.original: The food produced by a field of potatoes is not inferior in quantity to that produced by a field of rice, and much superior to what is produced by a field of wheat. Twelve thousand weight of potatoes from an acre of land is not a greater produce than two thousand weight of wheat. The food or solid nourishment, indeed, which can be drawn from each of those two plants, is not altogether in proportion to their weight, on account of the watery nature of potatoes. Allowing, however, half the weight of this root to go to water, a very large allowance, such an acre of potatoes will still produce six thousand weight of solid nourishment, three times the quantity produced by the acre of wheat. An acre of potatoes is cultivated with less expense than an acre of wheat; the fallow, which generally precedes the sowing of wheat, more than compensating the hoeing and other extraordinary culture which is always given to potatoes. Should this root ever become in any part of Europe, like rice in some rice countries, the common and favourite vegetable food of the people, so as to occupy the same proportion of the lands in tillage, which wheat and other sorts of grain for human food do at present, the same quantity of cultivated land would maintain a much greater number of people; and the labourers being generally fed with potatoes, a greater surplus would remain after replacing all the stock, and maintaining all the labour employed in cultivation. A greater share of this surplus, too, would belong to the landlord. Population would increase, and rents would rise much beyond what they are at present.
p48.zh: 马铃薯田生产的粮食数量不低于稻田生产的粮食,而且比小麦田生产的粮食数量要高得多。 从一亩土地得到的12 000磅的土豆,其产量并不大于2 000磅小麦。 实际上,从这两种植物中的每一种植物中都能得到的食物或固体营养,由于马铃薯的水性,与其重量不完全相称。 然而,允许这种根子的一半重量去水,非常大的量度,这样一亩的土豆仍然会产生六千重量的固体营养,是小麦亩产的三倍.种植一亩马铃薯的费用比一亩小麦要少;通常在播种小麦之前的落叶菜比补偿马铃薯的蹄食和其他特殊文化还要多。 如果这种根子成为欧洲任何地方的稻谷,如一些稻谷国家的稻米,人民所喜爱的共同蔬菜食品,以便占有目前小麦和其他种类的粮食用于人类粮食的同样比例的耕地,那么,同样数量的耕地将维持更多的人口;一般以马铃薯为食的工人,在取代所有库存之后,还有更大的剩余,并维持种植中的所有劳动力。这笔盈余的更大份额也属于房东。人口将增加,租金将远远超出目前水平。

p49.original: The land which is fit for potatoes, is fit for almost every other useful vegetable. If they occupied the same proportion of cultivated land which corn does at present, they would regulate, in the same manner, the rent of the greater part of other cultivated land.
p49.zh: 适合马铃薯的土地,几乎适合其他所有有用的蔬菜。 如果玉米目前占有的耕地比例相同,它们将以同样的方式管制其他耕地的大部分的租金。

p50.original: In some parts of Lancashire, it is pretended, I have been told, that bread of oatmeal is a heartier food for labouring people than wheaten bread, and I have frequently heard the same doctrine held in Scotland. I am, however, somewhat doubtful of the truth of it. The common people in Scotland, who are fed with oatmeal, are in general neither so strong nor so handsome as the same rank of people in England, who are fed with wheaten bread. They neither work so well, nor look so well; and as there is not the same difference between the people of fashion in the two countries, experience would seem to shew, that the food of the common people in Scotland is not so suitable to the human constitution as that of their neighbours of the same rank in England. But it seems to be otherwise with potatoes. The chairmen, porters, and coal-heavers in London, and those unfortunate women who live by prostitution, the strongest men and the most beautiful women perhaps in the British dominions, are said to be, the greater part of them, from the lowest rank of people in Ireland, who are generally fed with this root. No food can afford a more decisive proof of its nourishing quality, or of its being peculiarly suitable to the health of the human constitution.
p50.zh: 在兰卡西雷的一些地区,有人假装,我被告知,燕麦面包比小麦面包更能为劳苦的人们提供甜美的食物,我经常听到在苏格兰所持的同样理论。 然而,我有点怀疑它的真实性。苏格兰的普通人,以燕麦为食,一般来说,他们既不强壮,也不英俊,不像英国的同级人,他们以麦片面包为食. 他们的工作并不好,看起来也不好;而且由于两国时尚人民之间没有同样的区别,经验似乎会显现出来,苏格兰的普通人民的食物并不像他们在英格兰的同级邻居的食物那样适合人类宪法. 但是,它似乎不是与马铃薯。 据说,伦敦的主席、搬运工和拾煤工人,以及那些靠卖淫生活、最强壮的男子和最美丽的妇女,都是爱尔兰最底层的人,他们中的大部分人一般都以这种根茎为食。任何食物都无法更决定性地证明它的营养质量,或证明它特别适合人类宪法的健康。

p51.original: It is difficult to preserve potatoes through the year, and impossible to store them like corn, for two or three years together. The fear of not being able to sell them before they rot, discourages their cultivation, and is, perhaps, the chief obstacle to their ever becoming in any great country, like bread, the principal vegetable food of all the different ranks of the people.
p51.zh: 很难全年保存土豆,不可能像玉米一样储存,两三年在一起。害怕无法在腐烂前出售它们,阻止了它们的种植,或许是它们在任何伟大国家中成为的主要障碍,就像面包一样,是所有不同阶层人民的主要蔬菜食品。

p52.original: PART II.--Of the Produce of Land, which sometimes does, and sometimes does not, afford Rent.
p52.zh: 第二部分 土地生产,有时支付租金,有时支付不起租金。

p53.original: Human food seems to be the only produce of land, which always and necessarily affords some rent to the landlord. Other sorts of produce sometimes may, and sometimes may not, according to different circumstances.
p53.zh: 人类食物似乎是土地的唯一产物,它总是而且必然会给地主一些租金. 其他种类的产品有时可能,有时可能不会,因为情况不同。

p54.original: After food, clothing and lodging are the two great wants of mankind.
p54.zh: 食物、衣物和住处是人类的两大需求。

p55.original: Land, in its original rude state, can afford the materials of clothing and lodging to a much greater number of people than it can feed. In its improved state, it can sometimes feed a greater number of people than it can supply with those materials; at least in the way in which they require them, and are willing to pay for them. In the one state, therefore, there is always a superabundance of these materials, which are frequently, upon that account, of little or no value. In the other, there is often a scarcity, which necessarily augments their value. In the one state, a great part of them is thrown away as useless and the price of what is used is considered as equal only to the labour and expense of fitting it for use, and can, therefore, afford no rent to the landlord. In the other, they are all made use of, and there is frequently a demand for more than can be had. Somebody is always willing to give more for every part of them, than what is sufficient to pay the expense of bringing them to market. Their price, therefore, can always afford some rent to the landlord.
p55.zh: 土地原为粗鲁的土地,可以负担更多的人所买的衣物和住宿材料,而不能供养。在其改善的状态下,它有时能养活比它能供应那些材料更多的人;至少是用他们需要这些材料的方式,并且愿意支付它们的费用. 因此,在一个州,这些材料总是超量的,从这个角度讲,这些材料的价值往往很小或根本没有价值。 另一方面,往往缺乏资源,这必然会增加它们的价值。在一个州,其中很大一部分被丢弃,认为是无用,而所使用的价格被认为仅等同于装配使用所需的劳动和费用,因此,无法负担房东的租金。 另一方面,它们都得到了利用,而且往往需要的超出所能拥有的范围。 有人总是愿意为其中的每一个部分付出更多的代价,而不是支付将其投入市场的费用。 因此,他们的价格总是可以向房东支付一些租金。

p56.original: The skins of the larger animals were the original materials of clothing. Among nations of hunters and shepherds, therefore, whose food consists chiefly in the flesh of those animals, everyman, by providing himself with food, provides himself with the materials of more clothing than he can wear. If there was no foreign commerce, the greater part of them would be thrown away as things of no value. This was probably the case among the hunting nations of North America, before their country was discovered by the Europeans, with whom they now exchange their surplus peltry, for blankets, fire-arms, and brandy, which gives it some value. In the present commercial state of the known world, the most barbarous nations, I believe, among whom land property is established, have some foreign commerce of this kind, and find among their wealthier neighbours such a demand for all the materials of clothing, which their land produces, and which can neither be wrought up nor consumed at home, as raises their price above what it costs to send them to those wealthier neighbours. It affords, therefore, some rent to the landlord. When the greater part of the Highland cattle were consumed on their own hills, the exportation of their hides made the most considerable article of the commerce of that country, and what they were exchanged for afforded some addition to the rent of the Highland estates. The wool of England, which in old times, could neither be consumed nor wrought up at home, found a market in the then wealthier and more industrious country of Flanders, and its price afforded something to the rent of the land which produced it. In countries not better cultivated than England was then, or than the Highlands of Scotland are now, and which had no foreign commerce, the materials of clothing would evidently be so superabundant, that a great part of them would be thrown away as useless, and no part could afford any rent to the landlord.
p56.zh: 较大动物的皮肤是衣物的原始材料. 因此,在猎人和牧羊人的国家中,他们的食物主要存在于这些动物的肉中,每个人都通过提供食物,为自己提供比自己所能穿的更多衣物的材料. 如果没有外国商业,则其中的较大部分会作为无价值的东西丢掉。 在北美的狩猎国中,也许是这样,在他们的国家被欧洲人发现之前,他们现在与欧洲人交换了多余的卵子,换毯子,火武器,和白兰地,这给了它一些价值. 在目前已知世界的商业状况中,最野蛮的国家,我认为,在其中建立土地财产的国家,有一些这种外国商业,并且在其较富裕的邻国中发现,对土地生产的所有衣物材料的需求如此之高,而且这些衣物既不能制造,也不能在国内消费,它们的价格高于向这些较富裕的邻国运送这些衣物的成本。 因此,它向房东提供一些租金。 当高地牛的大部分在自己的山丘上被食用时,其藏品的出口成为该国商业中最重要的一条,而他们用来换取的东西也给高地庄园的租金提供了一些额外的报酬.英国的羊毛在旧时既不能消费,也不能在家中生产,在当时比较富裕和更加勤奋的佛兰德斯国家找到了市场,其价格为土地的租金提供了某种价值。 在不比当时的英格兰,或比现在的苏格兰高地,又没有对外商业的国家,衣物材料显然会如此超乎寻常,以至于其中很大一部分会被丢弃,成为无用之物,任何一部分都无法负担房东的租金.

p57.original: The materials of lodging cannot always be transported to so great a distance as those of clothing, and do not so readily become an object of foreign commerce. When they are superabundant in the country which produces them, it frequently happens, even in the present commercial state of the world, that they are of no value to the landlord. A good stone quarry in the neighbourhood of London would afford a considerable rent. In many parts of Scotland and Wales it affords none. Barren timber for building is of great value in a populous and well-cultivated country, and the land which produces it affords a considerable rent. But in many parts of North America, the landlord would be much obliged to any body who would carry away the greater part of his large trees. In some parts of the Highlands of Scotland, the bark is the only part of the wood which, for want of roads and water-carriage, can be sent to market; the timber is left to rot upon the ground. When the materials of lodging are so superabundant, the part made use of is worth only the labour and expense of fitting it for that use. It affords no rent to the landlord, who generally grants the use of it to whoever takes the trouble of asking it. The demand of wealthier nations, however, sometimes enables him to get a rent for it. The paving of the streets of London has enabled the owners of some barren rocks on the coast of Scotland to draw a rent from what never afforded any before. The woods of Norway, and of the coasts of the Baltic, find a market in many parts of Great Britain, which they could not find at home, and thereby afford some rent to their proprietors.
p57.zh: 住宿材料不能总是被运送到远至服装材料,也不可能轻易成为外国商业的对象。 当它们在生产这些产品的国家非常繁多时,即使在世界目前的商业状况下,也经常发生它们对房东毫无价值的情况。伦敦街区的一座好采石场可以支付相当的租金. 在苏格兰和威尔士的许多地方,这种补贴是没有的。在一个人口众多和种植良好的国家,巴伦木材对建筑很有价值,生产这种木材的土地可支付相当的租金。 但是在北美的许多地方,地主将不得不承受任何将他大树的大部分带走的躯体. 在苏格兰高地的一些地区,树皮是木材中唯一因为缺少道路和水运而可以运往市场的部分;木材被留在地上腐烂. 当住宿材料如此丰富时,使用的部分只值为这种使用配备所需的劳力和费用。 它不给地主任何租金,地主一般会给予谁用它来烦恼地要求它的人使用. 然而,较富裕国家的要求有时使他能够为此获得租金。伦敦街道的铺设使苏格兰海岸一些贫瘠岩石的业主能够从以前从未有过的地皮中提取租金. 挪威的树林,以及波罗的海的海岸,在大不列颠的许多地方找到了一个市场,他们在家里找不到,因此他们负担了自己的业主的一些租金.

p58.original: Countries are populous, not in proportion to the number of people whom their produce can clothe and lodge, but in proportion to that of those whom it can feed. When food is provided, it is easy to find the necessary clothing and lodging. But though these are at hand, it may often be difficult to find food. In some parts of the British dominions, what is called a house may be built by one day's labour of one man. The simplest species of clothing, the skins of animals, require somewhat more labour to dress and prepare them for use. They do not, however, require a great deal. Among savage or barbarous nations, a hundredth, or little more than a hundredth part of the labour of the whole year, will be sufficient to provide them with such clothing and lodging as satisfy the greater part of the people. All the other ninety-nine parts are frequently no more than enough to provide them with food.
p58.zh: 各国人口众多,与其产品能够衣食和住宿的人数成比例,与其能够供养的人数成比例。食物供应后,很容易找到必要的衣物和住所。 但是,尽管这些东西已经到了手头,但往往很难找到食物。 在英国统治的一些地区,所谓房屋,可能由一天的劳役,一个人来建造. 最简单的服装种类,动物的皮肤,需要多少劳动才能穿好衣服和准备使用. 然而,它们并不需要大量资源。 在野蛮或野蛮的民族中,一年中一百分之一或一百分一点以上的劳动,将足以为他们提供满足大部分人民需要的衣物和住所。所有其他99个部分往往不足以为他们提供食物。

p59.original: But when, by the improvement and cultivation of land, the labour of one family can provide food for two, the labour of half the society becomes sufficient to provide food for the whole. The other half, therefore, or at least the greater part of them, can be employed in providing other things, or in satisfying the other wants and fancies of mankind. Clothing and lodging, household furniture, and what is called equipage, are the principal objects of the greater part of those wants and fancies. The rich man consumes no more food than his poor neighbour. In quality it may be very different, and to select and prepare it may require more labour and art; but in quantity it is very nearly the same. But compare the spacious palace and great wardrobe of the one, with the hovel and the few rags of the other, and you will be sensible that the difference between their clothing, lodging, and household furniture, is almost as great in quantity as it is in quality. The desire of food is limited in every man by the narrow capacity of the human stomach; but the desire of the conveniencies and ornaments of building, dress, equipage, and household furniture, seems to have no limit or certain boundary. Those, therefore, who have the command of more food than they themselves can consume, are always willing to exchange the surplus, or, what is the same thing, the price of it, for gratifications of this other kind. What is over and above satisfying the limited desire, is given for the amusement of those desires which cannot be satisfied, but seem to be altogether endless. The poor, in order to obtain food, exert themselves to gratify those fancies of the rich; and to obtain it more certainly, they vie with one another in the cheapness and perfection of their work. The number of workmen increases with the increasing quantity of food, or with the growing improvement and cultivation of the lands; and as the nature of their business admits of the utmost subdivisions of labour, the quantity of materials which they can work up, increases in a much greater proportion than their numbers. Hence arises a demand for every sort of material which human invention can employ, either usefully or ornamentally, in building, dress, equipage, or household furniture; for the fossils and minerals contained in the bowels of the earth, the precious metals, and the precious stones.
p59.zh: 但是,当通过土地的改良和耕种,一个家庭的劳动能够为两个家庭提供食物时,社会的一半的劳动就足以为整个家庭提供食物. 因此,另一半,或至少其中更大一部分,可以被用来提供其他东西,或满足人类的其他愿望和幻想。服装和住宿、家庭家具以及所谓的装备是这些需要和幻想中的大部分的主要物品。富人食之,不比贫邻多. 在质量上,它可能非常不同,为了选择和准备它可能需要更多的劳动和艺术;但数量上却几乎一样。 但是,比较一个的宽敞的宫殿和大衣, 与另一个的豪华和少许的布布, 你会明白他们的衣着,住宿,和家庭家具之间的差别, 几乎与质量一样大。每个人对食物的渴望都受到人类胃的狭窄能力的限制;但是,建筑,服装,装备,家俱的舒适和装饰的欲望似乎没有限制或一定的界限. 因此,那些拥有比他们自己能消耗的更多粮食的指挥权的人,总是愿意把剩余部分换掉,或者,什么是同样的东西,它的价格,来换取这种其他种类的满足.满足有限愿望之外的东西,是用来取悦那些不能满足但似乎完全无休止的欲望的。穷人为了获得食物,努力向富人倾斜;为了获得食物,他们彼此之间必然在廉价和完美的工作之中互相竞争。 随着粮食数量的增加,或随着土地的不断改良和耕种,工人人数也有所增加;随着他们的企业性质承认了劳动力中最大的分支,他们能够增加的材料数量,比他们的数量增加的比例要大得多。 因此,人们需要人类发明在建筑、服装、装备或家用家具方面可以有用或装饰地使用的各种材料;需要地球肠道中所含的化石和矿物、贵金属和宝石。

p60.original: Food is, in this manner, not only the original source of rent, but every other part of the produce of land which afterwards affords rent, derives that part of its value from the improvement of the powers of labour in producing food, by means of the improvement and cultivation of land.
p60.zh: 因此,粮食不仅是原始的租金来源,而且,在土地的所有其他部分,如果后来能支付租金,则通过改善和耕种土地,通过提高生产粮食的劳动力能力,获得粮食的部分价值。

p61.original: Those other parts of the produce of land, however, which afterwards afford rent, do not afford it always. Even in improved and cultivated countries, the demand for them is not always such as to afford a greater price than what is sufficient to pay the labour, and replace, together with its ordinary profits, the stock which must be employed in bringing them to market. Whether it is or is not such, depends upon different circumstances.
p61.zh: 然而,土地的其他部分在支付租金后,并不总能支付租金。即使在改良和种植的国家,对它们的需求并不总是能够支付比支付劳动力所支付的价格更高的价格,并且用普通利润来取代必须用来将其投入市场的股票。是否如此,取决于不同的情况。

p62.original: Whether a coal mine, for example, can afford any rent, depends partly upon its fertility, and partly upon its situation.
p62.zh: 例如,煤矿能否负担任何租金,部分取决于其生育率,部分取决于其状况。

p63.original: A mine of any kind may be said to be either fertile or barren, according as the quantity of mineral which can be brought from it by a certain quantity of labour, is greater or less than what can be brought by an equal quantity from the greater part of other mines of the same kind.
p63.zh: 任何种类的矿井都可以说是肥沃的或贫瘠的,因为通过一定数量的劳动力从矿井中可以带来的矿物质数量,大于或少于来自同类其他矿井较大部分的矿物质所能带来的矿物质数量。

p64.original: Some coal mines, advantageously situated, cannot be wrought on account of their barrenness. The produce does not pay the expense. They can afford neither profit nor rent.
p64.zh: 一些位于有利位置的煤矿不能因其贫瘠而形成。产品不支付费用。 他们既无力支付利润,也无力支付租金。

p65.original: There are some, of which the produce is barely sufficient to pay the labour, and replace, together with its ordinary profits, the stock employed in working them. They afford some profit to the undertaker of the work, but no rent to the landlord. They can be wrought advantageously by nobody but the landlord, who, being himself the undertaker of the work, gets the ordinary profit of the capital which he employs in it. Many coal mines in Scotland are wrought in this manner, and can be wrought in no other. The landlord will allow nobody else to work them without paying some rent, and nobody can afford to pay any.
p65.zh: 有些产品几乎不足以支付劳动力,它们除了普通利润之外,还取代了在生产这些产品时使用的股票。 他们给工程的承租人带来了一些利润,但是没有给房东的租金. 只有地主才能有利地创造这些财富,而地主本身是工程的承担者,他从中获得了他所雇用的资本的普通利润。苏格兰的许多煤矿都是以这种方式开采的,不可能以其他方式开采。房东不付房租就不允许其他人工作,没有人能付得起房租。

p66.original: Other coal mines in the same country, sufficiently fertile, cannot be wrought on account of their situation. A quantity of mineral, sufficient to defray the expense of working, could be brought from the mine by the ordinary, or even less than the ordinary quantity of labour: but in an inland country, thinly inhabited, and without either good roads or water-carriage, this quantity could not be sold.
p66.zh: 同一国家的其他煤矿,如果足够肥沃,则不能因其情况而兴建。一定数量的矿物质,足以支付劳动费用,一般人可以从矿中运出,甚至少于一般劳动力数量:但是在内陆国家,人烟稀少,没有良好的道路或水运,这种数量是不能出售的.

p67.original: Coals are a less agreeable fuel than wood: they are said too to be less wholesome. The expense of coals, therefore, at the place where they are consumed, must generally be somewhat less than that of wood.
p67.zh: 煤是一种比木材更不合适的燃料:据说它们也不太健康。 因此,煤炭在消费地点的费用一般必须略低于木材。

p68.original: The price of wood, again, varies with the state of agriculture, nearly in the same manner, and exactly for the same reason, as the price of cattle. In its rude beginnings, the greater part of every country is covered with wood, which is then a mere incumbrance, of no value to the landlord, who would gladly give it to any body for the cutting. As agriculture advances, the woods are partly cleared by the progress of tillage, and partly go to decay in consequence of the increased number of cattle. These, though they do not increase in the same proportion as corn, which is altogether the acquisition of human industry, yet multiply under the care and protection of men, who store up in the season of plenty what may maintain them in that of scarcity; who, through the whole year, furnish them with a greater quantity of food than uncultivated nature provides for them; and who, by destroying and extirpating their enemies, secure them in the free enjoyment of all that she provides. Numerous herds of cattle, when allowed to wander through the woods, though they do not destroy the old trees, hinder any young ones from coming up; so that, in the course of a century or two, the whole forest goes to ruin. The scarcity of wood then raises its price. It affords a good rent; and the landlord sometimes finds that he can scarce employ his best lands more advantageously than in growing barren timber, of which the greatness of the profit often compensates the lateness of the returns. This seems, in the present times, to be nearly the state of things in several parts of Great Britain, where the profit of planting is found to be equal to that of either corn or pasture. The advantage which the landlord derives from planting can nowhere exceed, at least for any considerable time, the rent which these could afford him; and in an inland country, which is highly cuitivated, it will frequently not fall much short of this rent. Upon the sea-coast of a well-improved country, indeed, if coals can conveniently be had for fuel, it may sometimes be cheaper to bring barren timber for building from less cultivated foreign countries than to raise it at home. In the new town of Edinburgh, built within these few years, there is not, perhaps, a single stick of Scotch timber.
p68.zh: 木价,又因农业状况而异,近乎同之,而正因之,与牛价同之.在其粗鲁的开端,每个国家的较大部分都覆盖着木头,而这种木头仅仅是一种积木,对地主来说毫无价值,地主愿意把它交给任何一具尸体用于切割. 随着农业的进步,森林部分地被耕作的进展所清除,部分地由于牛的数量增加而衰落。 这些粮食虽然与玉米的比例不同,而玉米完全是人类工业的获得,但在男人的照顾和保护下却增加了,男人在丰盛的季节里储存着可以维持其稀缺的粮食;他们全年向他们提供的粮食数量比未耕种的自然供应的多;他们摧毁和消灭敌人,使他们自由享受她提供的一切。无数牛群,当被允许在树林中徘徊时,虽然它们不破坏老树,却阻碍任何年轻人爬上去;这样,在一两个世纪的时间里,整个森林都变得一片废墟.木材的匮乏又提高了价格。 它能提供很好的租金;而地主有时发现,他可以少用他最好的土地,比种植贫瘠的木材更有利,其中利润的丰厚往往能补偿回报的迟到。 这在当今时代似乎几乎是大不列颠的几个地区的状况,在那里,种植的利润被认为与玉米或牧场的利润相等。地主从种植中获得的优势,至少在任何相当长的时间内,都不可能超过他们能够负担的租金;在一个高度合格、内地国家,这种租金往往不会大大低于租金。在一个改善良好的国家的海岸上,事实上,如果可以方便地用煤作为燃料,有时从较少种植的外国为建筑运送贫瘠的木材比在国内提炼要便宜。 在这几年里兴建的爱丁堡新城里,也许没有一根苏格兰木材。

p69.original: Whatever may be the price of wood, if that of coals is such that the expense of a coal fire is nearly equal to that of a wood one we may be assured, that at that place, and in these circumstances, the price of coals is as high as it can be. It seems to be so in some of the inland parts of England, particularly in Oxfordshire, where it is usual, even in the fires of the common people, to mix coals and wood together, and where the difference in the expense of those two sorts of fuel cannot, therefore, be very great. Coals, in the coal countries, are everywhere much below this highest price. If they were not, they could not bear the expense of a distant carriage, either by land or by water. A small quantity only could be sold; and the coal masters and the coal proprietors find it more for their interest to sell a great quantity at a price somewhat above the lowest, than a small quantity at the highest. The most fertile coal mine, too, regulates the price of coals at all the other mines in its neighbourhood. Both the proprietor and the undertaker of the work find, the one that he can get a greater rent, the other that he can get a greater profit, by somewhat underselling all their neighbours. Their neighbours are soon obliged to sell at the same price, though they cannot so well afford it, and though it always diminishes, and sometimes takes away altogether, both their rent and their profit. Some works are abandoned altogether; others can afford no rent, and can be wrought only by the proprietor.
p69.zh: 无论木材的价格如何,如果煤炭的价格是几乎等于一个木柴的费用,我们可以保证,在那个地方,在这种情况下,煤炭的价格是尽可能高的. 在英国的一些内陆地区,特别是在牛津郡,似乎如此,这里通常甚至普通百姓的火灾中,都把煤和木混在一起,因此这两种燃料的成本差别不可能很大. 在煤炭国家,煤炭价格远远低于这一最高价格。 如果不是,他们就无法承担远方运输的费用,无论是通过陆路还是水路。少量只能出售;煤主和煤炭所有者认为以略高于最低的价格出售大量数量比在最高价格出售少量更符合他们的利益。 最肥沃的煤矿也对其附近其他所有矿山的煤价进行调节.工作主人和承业者都发现,一个他可以得到更大的租金,另一个他可以得到更大的利润,通过略微降低他们所有邻居的销售. 他们的邻居很快不得不以同样的价格出售,尽管他们负担不起,尽管这种价格总是减少,有时甚至完全夺走他们的租金和利润。 有些工程被完全废弃;另一些工程没有租金,只能由业主建造。

p70.original: The lowest price at which coals can be sold for any considerable time, is, like that of all other commodities, the price which is barely sufficient to replace, together with its ordinary profits, the stock which must be employed in bringing them to market. At a coal mine for which the landlord can get no rent, but, which he must either work himself or let it alone altogether, the price of coals must generally be nearly about this price.
p70.zh: 煤炭在任何相当长的时间内都可以出售的最低价格是,与所有其他商品一样,这一价格几乎不足以与普通利润一起取代必须用来将煤炭带入市场的股票。 在地主不能得到租金的煤矿,但是,他必须自己工作,或完全不要工作,煤的价格一般必须接近这一价格。

p71.original: Rent, even where coals afford one, has generally a smaller share in their price than in that of most other parts of the rude produce of land. The rent of an estate above ground, commonly amounts to what is supposed to be a third of the gross produce; and it is generally a rent certain and independent of the occasional variations in the crop. In coal mines, a fifth of the gross produce is a very great rent, a tenth the common rent; and it is seldom a rent certain, but depends upon the occasional variations in the produce. These are so great, that in a country where thirty years purchase is considered as a moderate price for the property of a landed estate, ten years purchase is regarded as a good price for that of a coal mine.
p71.zh: 租借,即使煤炭买得起租借,其价格份额一般也比其他大部分粗鲁的地产的租借要小。地上庄园的租金通常相当于应占总产值的三分之一;一般是一定的租金,独立于作物偶尔变异。 在煤矿中,总产值的五分之一是非常高的租金,是普通租金的十分之一;它很少是租金的确定,但取决于产量的不定期变化。这些都是巨大的,在一个三十年购买被视为一个土地财产中温和价格的国家,十年购买被视为一个煤矿的良好价格。

p72.original: The value of a coal mine to the proprietor, frequently depends as much upon its situation as upon its fertility. That of a metallic mine depends more upon its fertility, and less upon its situation. The coarse, and still more the precious metals, when separated from the ore, are so valuable, that they can generally bear the expense of a very long land, and of the most distant sea carriage. Their market is not confined to the countries in the neighbourhood of the mine, but extends to the whole world. The copper of Japan makes an article of commerce in Europe; the iron of Spain in that of Chili and Peru. The silver of Peru finds its way, not only to Europe, but from Europe to China.
p72.zh: 煤矿对矿主的价值往往取决于其状况和其生产力。金属矿更取决于其肥力,而较少取决于其状况。粗 ⁇ ,而更贵重的金属,在与矿石分离时,其价值如此之高,一般可以负担很长的陆地和最远的海上运输的费用.它们的市场不仅限于矿区邻国,而是扩展到全世界。 日本的青铜器在欧洲制造了一条商业物品;在奇利和秘鲁的铁器中制造了西班牙的铁. 秘鲁的银器找到它的道路,不仅通往欧洲,而且从欧洲到中国.

p73.original: The price of coals in Westmoreland or Shropshire can have little effect on their price at Newcastle; and their price in the Lionnois can have none at all. The productions of such distant coal mines can never be brought into competition with one another. But the productions of the most distant metallic mines frequently may, and in fact commonly are.
p73.zh: 威斯特摩兰或施罗普郡的煤炭价格对纽卡斯尔的煤炭价格影响不大;在利诺伊斯的煤炭价格则完全没有. 这种遥远的煤矿的生产永远不能相互竞争。 但是,最遥远的金属矿的产量可能而且实际上通常都是如此。

p74.original: The price, therefore, of the coarse, and still more that of the precious metals, at the most fertile mines in the world, must necessarily more or less affect their price at every other in it. The price of copper in Japan must have some influence upon its price at the copper mines in Europe. The price of silver in Peru, or the quantity either of labour or of other goods which it will purchase there, must have some influence on its price, not only at the silver mines of Europe, but at those of China. After the discovery of the mines of Peru, the silver mines of Europe were, the greater part of them, abandoned. The value of silver was so much reduced, that their produce could no longer pay the expense of working them, or replace, with a profit, the food, clothes, lodging, and other necessaries which were consumed in that operation. This was the case, too, with the mines of Cuba and St. Domingo, and even with the ancient mines of Peru, after the discovery of those of Potosi. The price of every metal, at every mine, therefore, being regulated in some measure by its price at the most fertile mine in the world that is actually wrought, it can, at the greater part of mines, do very little more than pay the expense of working, and can seldom afford a very high rent to the landlord. Rent accordingly, seems at the greater part of mines to have but a small share in the price of the coarse, and a still smaller in that of the precious metals. Labour and profit make up the greater part of both.
p74.zh: 因此,粗金属的价格,以及更多的贵金属的价格,在世界上最肥沃的矿场,必然会对其价格产生很大或较小的影响。 日本的铜价对于其在欧洲铜矿的价格一定有一定的影响. 秘鲁的白银价格,或者说它将要在那里购买的劳力或其他商品的数量,必须对其价格产生一定的影响,不仅在欧洲的白银矿,而且在中国的银矿. 在秘鲁矿发现后,欧洲的银矿被废弃,其中较大的部分被废弃.白银的价值大大降低,其产品无法支付工作费用,或用利润取代在这项业务中消耗的食物、衣服、住宿和其他必需品。 古巴和圣塔的矿井也是如此。 多明戈,甚至与秘鲁的古代矿山一起,在发现波托西的矿山之后. 因此,每一种金属的价格,在每一个矿场,都在某种程度上受到它实际上在世界上最肥沃的矿场的价格的管制,在矿场的大部分,它只能支付工作费用,而且很少能支付房东的非常高的租金。 因此,在矿山的大部分地区,粗金刚石的价格似乎只有很小的份额,而在贵金属方面,租金却更小。劳动和利润占了两者的较大部分。

p75.original: A sixth part of the gross produce may be reckoned the average rent of the tin mines of Cornwall, the most fertile that are known in the world, as we are told by the Rev. Mr. Borlace, vice-warden of the stannaries. Some, he says, afford more, and some do not afford so much. A sixth part of the gross produce is the rent, too, of several very fertile lead mines in Scotland.
p75.zh: 毛产的第六部分可以算作康沃尔锡矿的平均租金,正如《Rev》告诉我们的那样,康沃尔锡矿是世界上最肥沃的。先生,请问您是博莱斯,史丹那的副手 他说,有些人付得起更多,有些人付不起这么多。毛产的第六部分是苏格兰几个非常肥沃的铅矿的租金。

p76.original: In the silver mines of Peru, we are told by Frezier and Ulloa, the proprietor frequently exacts no other acknowledgment from the undertaker of the mine, but that he will grind the ore at his mill, paying him the ordinary multure or price of grinding.
