Under this system of management, it is evident, even that part of the lands of Scotland which is capable of good cultivation, could produce but little in comparison of what it may be capable of producing. But how disadvantageous soever this system may appear, yet, before the Union, the low price of cattle seems to have rendered it almost unavoidable. If, notwithstanding a great rise in the price, it still continues to prevail through a considerable part of the country, it is owing in many places, no doubt, to ignorance and attachment to old customs, but, in most places, to the unavoidable obstructions which the natural course of things opposes to the immediate or speedy establishment of a better system: first, to the poverty of the tenants, to their not having yet had time to acquire a stock of cattle sufficient to cultivate their lands more completely, the same rise of price, which would render it advantageous for them to maintain a greater stock, rendering it more difficult for them to acquire it; and, secondly, to their not having yet had time to put their lands in condition to maintain this greater stock properly, supposing they were capable of acquiring it. The increase of stock and the improvement of land are two events which must go hand in hand, and of which the one can nowhere much outrun the other. Without some increase of stock, there can be scarce any improvement of land, but there can be no considerable increase of stock, but in consequence of a considerable improvement of land; because otherwise the land could not maintain it. These natural obstructions to the establishment of a better system, cannot be removed but by a long course of frugality and industry; and half a century or a century more, perhaps, must pass away before the old system, which is wearing out gradually, can be completely abolished through all the different parts of the country. Of all the commercial advantages, however, which Scotland has derived from the Union with England, this rise in the price of cattle is, perhaps, the greatest. It has not only raised the value of all highland estates, but it has, perhaps, been the principal cause of the improvement of the low country.
p201.zh: 直到牛的价格达到这个高度, 大部分土地,甚至那些能种植最多土地的土地, 似乎都难以完全耕种。在所有远离任何城镇、无法从中搬运粪肥的农场中,即在每一个广大国家的农场中,耕地数量必须与农场本身生产的粪肥数量成比例;这也必须与农场所养牛的数量成比例。土地有manued的,要么是在上面放羊,要么是在马厩里喂牛,从那里去放粪。惟牛之价足以既付耕地之租,又得其利,则农夫无以牧之;而农夫亦无以牧之,而于马厩中养之. 只有经过改良和耕地的产量,才能在马厩中喂养牛;因为收集稀薄和分散的废物和未经改良的土地的产量,需要太多的劳力,而且费用太高。 因此,牛的价钱不足以支付改良和地产,当他们被允许放牧时,价格仍然不足以支付这些产物,而必须用大量的额外劳力来收集这些产物,并将它们带进马厩。 因此,在这种情况下,在马厩里,没有比耕作所需的更多的利润可以喂养的牛。但这些肥料永远买不起,无法保持他们能够耕种的所有土地的正常状况。 他们所付的钱,如果不足以用于整个农场,自然将留给最有利或最方便使用的土地;最肥沃的土地,或也许在农场附近的土地。 因此,这些土地将保持良好状态,适于耕作。其余部分则被允许埋藏废物,除了一些悲惨的牧场外,其他的牧场都很少,仅够养活几头破碎、半饿的牛;农场虽然按其完全种植所需的数量过多,但往往按其实际产量过多。 然而,这片荒地的一部分,在经过六七年的这种恶劣放牧之后,可能会被犁起来,当它可能生产出一棵贫瘠的作物或两棵劣质的燕麦,或某种其他粗粮时;然后,由于已经完全耗尽,它必须象以前一样再休息和放牧,另一部分则又被犁起来,然后又以同样的方式耗尽和再休息。 因此,在联盟之前,这种管理体制是整个苏格兰低层国家的总体管理制度。一直保持良好管理、状况良好的土地很少超过整个农场的第三或第四部分,有时也不到第五或第六部分。其余的人从未受过管理,但其中一部分人却在自己身上,尽管如此,经常耕种和耗尽。 在这种管理制度下,显然,即使是能够种植良种的苏格兰部分土地也可以生产,但与它可能生产的土地相比却很少。 但是无论这种制度如何不利,在联盟面前,牛的低价似乎使它几乎无法避免。 尽管价格大幅上涨,但价格仍然通过该国相当大一部分地区持续上涨,这无疑是由于许多地方的无知和对旧习俗的依恋,但是在多数地方,自然过程必然会阻碍立即或迅速建立更好的制度:第一,由于租户的贫困,他们还没有时间购买足够充分耕种其土地的牲畜,同样的价格上涨,使得他们能够维持更大的牲畜,使他们更难获得这些牲畜;第二,由于他们还没有时间让自己的土地能够适当维持这一更大的牲畜,假定他们有能力获得这些牲畜。种群的增加和土地的改善是必须同时发生的两个事件,其中之一无处可逃。种群不增加,土地就很少有改善,但种群不会大量增加,而是由于土地有相当大的改善;否则土地就无法维持。 这些阻碍建立更好制度的自然障碍,不能消除,只能通过长期的节俭和工业;半个世纪或更一个世纪以后,也许必须先消亡,然后才能通过全国各地逐渐消退的旧制度彻底废除. 然而,在苏格兰从与英格兰的联盟中获得的所有商业优势中,牛的这种价格上涨或许是最大的。 它不仅提高了所有高地庄园的价值,而且也许是低地国家改善的主要原因。

p202.original: In all new colonies, the great quantity of waste land, which can for many years be applied to no other purpose but the feeding of cattle, soon renders them extremely abundant; and in every thing great cheapness is the necessary consequence of great abundance. Though all the cattle of the European colonies in America were originally carried from Europe, they soon multiplied so much there, and became of so little value, that even horses were allowed to run wild in the woods, without any owner thinking it worth while to claim them. It must be a long time after the first establishment of such colonies, before it can become profitable to feed cattle upon the produce of cultivated land. The same causes, therefore, the want of manure, and the disproportion between the stock employed in cultivation and the land which it is destined to cultivate, are likely to introduce there a system of husbandry, not unlike that which still continues to take place in so many parts of Scotland. Mr Kalm, the Swedish traveller, when he gives an account of the husbandry of some of the English colonies in North America, as he found it in 1749, observes, accordingly, that he can with difficulty discover there the character of the English nation, so well skilled in all the different branches of agriculture. They make scarce any manure for their corn fields, he says; but when one piece of ground has been exhausted by continual cropping, they clear and cultivate another piece of fresh land; and when that is exhausted, proceed to a third. Their cattle are allowed to wander through the woods and other uncultivated grounds, where they are half-starved; having long ago extirpated almost all the annual grasses, by cropping them too early in the spring, before they had time to form their flowers, or to shed their seeds. {Kalm's Travels, vol 1, pp. 343, 344.} The annual grasses were, it seems, the best natural grasses in that part of North America; and when the Europeans first settled there, they used to grow very thick, and to rise three or four feet high. A piece of ground which, when he wrote, could not maintain one cow, would in former times, he was assured, have maintained four, each of which would have given four times the quantity of milk which that one was capable of giving. The poorness of the pasture had, in his opinion, occasioned the degradation of their cattle, which degenerated sensibly from me generation to another. They were probably not unlike that stunted breed which was common all over Scotland thirty or forty years ago, and which is now so much mended through the greater part of the low country, not so much by a change of the breed, though that expedient has been employed in some places, as by a more plentiful method of feeding them.
p202.zh: 在所有新的殖民地中,大量荒地,多年来只能用于其他目的,而只能用于喂养牛群,这些荒地很快就变得极为丰富;在每一方面,大便宜都是大丰产的必要后果. 虽然美国欧洲殖民地的所有牛最初都是从欧洲运来的,但很快它们就在那里倍增了,变得价值极小,以至于连马都允许在树林中野跑,没有任何主人认为在要求它们的同时值得. 在第一次建立这种殖民地之后,它必须很长一段时间,才能在耕地的产地上养牛。 因此,同样的原因,即缺乏肥料,以及种植中所使用的牲畜与它所要耕种的土地之间的不成比例,都有可能引入一种畜牧业制度,这与苏格兰许多地区仍在实行的制度不相上下。 瑞典旅行家卡尔姆先生在1749年发现的他叙述北美一些英国殖民地的畜牧业时,因此指出他很难在那里发现英格兰民族的特征,在农业的所有不同分支中都技术非常熟练. 他说,他们为自己的玉米田而缺肥;当一块土地因不断耕种而耗尽时,他们清理和耕种另一块新土地;当土地用尽时,他们就进入三分之一。 他们的牛被允许在树林和其他未开垦的土地上徘徊,在那里他们半饿;很久以前,他们几乎把一年一度的草种都除去了,在春天过早地将其收割,在他们有时间形成花朵之前,或者在放出种子. {卡尔姆的旅记,第1卷,pp.343, 344.}每年的草似乎都是北美那个地区最好的天然草;当欧洲人第一次定居在那里时,它们曾经生长非常厚,并且上升了三四英尺高. 在他写作时无法维持一头牛的一块地上,他可以放心,在以前的时代,他可以维持四只,每只地上会提供四倍于他所能给予的牛奶。 他认为,牧场的贫瘠导致他们的牲畜退化,这使我的一代人明智地退化。 它们可能与30或40年前苏格兰各地常见的发育不良的品种不同,这种品种现在在低地国家的大部分地区都得到了很大改善,而不是由于品种的改变,尽管这种迅速性在有些地方得到了利用,比如通过一种更丰满的喂养方法。

p203.original: Though it is late, therefore, in the progress of improvement, before cattle can bring such a price as to render it profitable to cultivate land for the sake of feeding them; yet of all the different parts which compose this second sort of rude produce, they are perhaps the first which bring this price; because, till they bring it, it seems impossible that improvement can be brought near even to that degree of perfection to which it has arrived in many parts of Europe.
p203.zh: 因此,虽然在改进方面已经很晚了,但牛尚未能够带来这样一个价格,使它能有利可图地耕种,以养活它们;然而,在构成第二类粗鲁农产品的所有不同部分中,它们或许是第一个带来这种价格的;因为,在它们带来这种价格之前,即使达到它在欧洲许多地方达到的完美程度,也似乎也不可能带来这种改善。

p204.original: As cattle are among the first, so perhaps venison is among the last parts of this sort of rude produce which bring this price. The price of venison in Great Britain, how extravagant soever it may appear, is not near sufficient to compensate the expense of a deer park, as is well known to all those who have had any experience in the feeding of deer. If it was otherwise, the feeding of deer would soon become an article of common farming, in the same manner as the feeding of those small birds, called turdi, was among the ancient Romans. Varro and Columella assure us, that it was a most profitable article. The fattening of ortolans, birds of passage which arrive lean in the country, is said to be so in some parts of France. If venison continues in fashion, and the wealth and luxury of Great Britain increase as they have done for some time past, its price may very probably rise still higher than it is at present.
p204.zh: 因为牛是第一种, 所以也许食肉动物 是这种粗鲁的产物的最后一部分 带来了这个价格。 大不列颠的食肉价格,无论它看起来多么奢侈,都不足以补偿鹿园的费用,所有有喂鹿经验的人都知道这一点. 如果不然,鹿的喂养很快就会成为普通农耕的一条,与那些被称为 ⁇ 的小型鸟类的喂养一样,属于古罗马人之列.Varro和Columella向我们保证,这是一篇最赚钱的文章。 据说,在法国的一些地区,奥托兰的肥胖现象,即到达法国的鸟类,是这种情况。 如果venison在时尚上继续下去,大不列颠的财富和奢侈品也像过去一段时间一样增加,那么它的价格很可能仍然比现在更高.

p205.original: Between that period in the progress of improvement, which brings to its height the price of so necessary an article as cattle, and that which brings to it the price of such a superfluity as venison, there is a very long interval, in the course of which many other sorts of rude produce gradually arrive at their highest price, some sooner and some later, according to different circumstances.
p205.zh: 在此期间,在不断改进的过程中,使牛这种必要物品的价格达到最高水平,而使牛这种超级富力的价格达到最高水平,这两者之间,间隔很长,在此期间,许多其他种类的无礼产品逐渐达到最高价格,有的更早,有的更晚,视不同情况而定.

p206.original: Thus, in every farm, the offals of the barn and stable will maintain a certain number of poultry. These, as they are fed with what would otherwise be lost, are a mere save-all; and as they cost the farmer scarce any thing, so he can afford to sell them for very little. Almost all that he gets is pure gain, and their price can scarce be so low as to discourage him from feeding this number. But in countries ill cultivated, and therefore but thinly inhabited, the poultry, which are thus raised without expense, are often fully sufficient to supply the whole demand. In this state of things, therefore, they are often as cheap as butcher's meat, or any other sort of animal food. But the whole quantity of poultry which the farm in this manner produces without expense, must always be much smaller than the whole quantity of butcher's meat which is reared upon it; and in times of wealth and luxury, what is rare, with only nearly equal merit, is always preferred to what is common. As wealth and luxury increase, therefore, in consequence of improvement and cultivation, the price of poultry gradually rises above that of butcher's meat, till at last it gets so high, that it becomes profitable to cultivate land for the sake of feeding them. When it has got to this height, it cannot well go higher. If it did, more land would soon be turned to this purpose. In several provinces of France, the feeding of poultry is considered as a very important article in rural economy, and sufficiently profitable to encourage the farmer to raise a considerable quantity of Indian corn and buckwheat for this purpose. A middling farmer will there sometimes have four hundred fowls in his yard. The feeding of poultry seems scarce yet to be generally considered as a matter of so much importance in England. They are certainly, however, dearer in England than in France, as England receives considerable supplies from France. In the progress of improvements, the period at which every particular sort of animal food is dearest, must naturally be that which immediately precedes the general practice of cultivating land for the sake of raising it. For some time before this practice becomes general, the scarcity must necessarily raise the price. After it has become general, new methods of feeding are commonly fallen upon, which enable the farmer to raise upon the same quantity of ground a much greater quantity of that particular sort of animal food. The plenty not only obliges him to sell cheaper, but, in consequence of these improvements, he can afford to sell cheaper; for if he could not afford it, the plenty would not be of long continuance. It has been probably in this manner that the introduction of clover, turnips, carrots, cabbages, etc. has contributed to sink the common price of butcher's meat in the London market, somewhat below what it was about the beginning of the last century.
p206.zh: 因此,在每一个农场,谷仓的地皮和稳定地会维持一定数量的家禽. 这些东西,因为吃到本来会损失的东西,只是一笔储蓄;他们使农民失去任何东西,因此,他可以买得起这些东西,但卖得很少。 他得到的几乎都是纯净的收益,他们的价格可能很少,以至于阻止他喂食这个数字. 但是,在种植不良、因而居住稀少的国家,家禽往往完全能够满足全部需求,而家禽的饲养却不需花费费用。 因此,在这种状态下,它们往往和屠夫的肉一样便宜,或者其他任何种类的动物食物. 但农场以这种方式生产的全部家禽数量必须总是比养殖的屠夫肉数量小得多;在财富和奢侈的时候,只有几乎同等的功绩才稀有的,总是比常见的要好。 因此,随着财富和奢侈品的增加,由于改良和种植,家禽的价格逐渐高于屠宰肉的价格,直到最终达到如此高的地步,为了养活它们而耕种土地变得有利可图. 当它达到这个高度时,它不能再高了。 如果是这样的话,不久就会有更多的土地转向这个目的. 在法国的几个省份,家禽的喂养被认为是农村经济中非常重要的一条东西,而且利润足以鼓励农民为此目的饲养大量印度玉米和大麦。 一个杂务农夫有时会在他的院子里放着四百只小鸟家禽的喂养似乎很少,但在英国,人们一般认为这是一个非常重要的问题。 然而,他们肯定在英国比在法国更加亲切,因为英国从法国得到大量物资. 在改进过程中,每一类动物食物最珍贵的时期,自然必须是紧接在为养殖土地而耕种的一般做法之前的时期。 在这种做法变得普遍之前的一段时间里,稀缺性必然会提高价格。新的喂养方法在变得普遍之后,通常会遭到破坏,使农民能够在同样数量的地上增加这种动物食物的数量。 这些财富不仅迫使他出售更便宜,而且由于这些改进,他能够买得起更便宜的商品;因为如果他买不起,这些财富不会长久持续下去。可能正是以这种方式,引进丁香,萝卜,胡萝卜,小白菜等,使得屠夫肉类在伦敦市场的共同价格下沉,略低于上个世纪初的大致价格.

p207.original: The hog, that finds his food among ordure, and greedily devours many things rejected by every other useful animal, is, like poultry, originally kept as a save-all. As long as the number of such animals, which can thus be reared at little or no expense, is fully sufficient to supply the demand, this sort of butcher's meat comes to market at a much lower price than any other. But when the demand rises beyond what this quantity can supply, when it becomes necessary to raise food on purpose for feeding and fattening hogs, in the same manner as for feeding and fattening other cattle, the price necessarily rises, and becomes proportionably either higher or lower than that of other butcher's meat, according as the nature of the country, and the state of its agriculture, happen to render the feeding of hogs more or less expensive than that of other cattle. In France, according to Mr Buffon, the price of pork is nearly equal to that of beef. In most parts of Great Britain it is at present somewhat higher.
p207.zh: 这只猪, 发现他的食物在矿石中, 贪婪地吞噬了许多东西 被其他有用的动物拒绝, 和家禽一样, 最初被保存为一种储蓄。 只要这种动物的数量能够以很少或零花钱养活,就足以满足需求,这种屠夫的肉类就以比其他任何一种要低得多的价格进入市场. 但是,当需求增加,超出这个数量所能供应的范围时,当为了喂养和肥猪而需要故意饲养食物,与喂养和肥其他牛一样,价格必然会上升,并且根据国家的性质及其农业状况,变得比其他肉类的肉类有比例地高或低,恰好使喂养猪比其他牛多或少昂贵. 在法国,根据Buffon先生的说法,猪肉的价格几乎相当于牛肉的价格. 在大不列颠的多数地区,目前情况略高一些。

p208.original: The great rise in the price both of hogs and poultry, has, in Great Britain, been frequently imputed to the diminution of the number of cottagers and other small occupiers of land; an event which has in every part of Europe been the immediate forerunner of improvement and better cultivation, but which at the same time may have contributed to raise the price of those articles, both somewhat sooner and somewhat faster than it would otherwise have risen. As the poorest family can often maintain a cat or a dog without any expense, so the poorest occupiers of land can commonly maintain a few poultry, or a sow and a few pigs, at very little. The little offals of their own table, their whey, skimmed milk, and butter milk, supply those animals with a part of their food, and they find the rest in the neighbouring fields, without doing any sensible damage to any body. By diminishing the number of those small occupiers, therefore, the quantity of this sort of provisions, which is thus produced at little or no expense, must certainly have been a good deal diminished, and their price must consequently have been raised both sooner and faster than it would otherwise have risen. Sooner or later, however, in the progress of improvement, it must at any rate have risen to the utmost height to which it is capable of rising; or to the price which pays the labour and expense of cultivating the land which furnishes them with food, as well as these are paid upon the greater part of other cultivated land.
p208.zh: 在大不列颠,猪和家禽价格的大幅上涨常常被归结为家庭主妇和其他小块土地占有者人数的减少;在欧洲各地,这一事件是改良和改良种植的直接先驱,但与此同时,这也许有助于提高这些物品的价格,这比本来会提高的要早一些,也比本来会提高的要快一些。 由于最贫穷的家庭往往可以不用任何费用养猫或养狗,所以土地的最贫穷的占有者通常可以养几只家禽,或养一头母猪和几头猪,但很少. 他们自己的桌子上的小外衣,他们的小毛, 滑雪牛奶,和黄油牛奶, 供应这些动物的一部分食物, 他们发现其余的在邻近的田地里, 没有给任何身体造成任何合理的伤害。 因此,通过减少这些小的占领者的数目,这种规定的数量 -- -- 因此很少或不花费任何费用 -- -- 肯定已经大大降低了,因此,它们的价格必须比本来会上涨的更快和更快地上涨。 然而,在改进过程中,它迟早必须达到能够达到的最高水平;或者达到支付劳动力和耕作费用的价格,而耕种土地为他们提供粮食,而这些土地则在大部分其他耕地上支付。

p209.original: The business of the dairy, like the feeding of hogs and poultry, is originally carried on as a save-all. The cattle necessarily kept upon the farm produce more milk than either the rearing of their own young, or the consumption of the farmer's family requires; and they produce most at one particular season. But of all the productions of land, milk is perhaps the most perishable. In the warm season, when it is most abundant, it will scarce keep four-and-twenty hours. The farmer, by making it into fresh butter, stores a small part of it for a week; by making it into salt butter, for a year; and by making it into cheese, he stores a much greater part of it for several years. Part of all these is reserved for the use of his own family; the rest goes to market, in order to find the best price which is to be had, and which can scarce be so low is to discourage him from sending thither whatever is over and above the use of his own family. If it is very low indeed, he will be likely to manage his dairy in a very slovenly and dirty manner, and will scarce, perhaps, think it worth while to have a particular room or building on purpose for it, but will suffer the business to be carried on amidst the smoke, filth, and nastiness of his own kitchen, as was the case of almost all the farmers' dairies in Scotland thirty or forty years ago, and as is the case of many of them still. The same causes which gradually raise the price of butcher's meat, the increase of the demand, and, in consequence of the improvement of the country, the diminution of the quantity which can be fed at little or no expense, raise, in the same manner, that of the produce of the dairy, of which the price naturally connects with that of butcher's meat, or with the expense of feeding cattle. The increase of price pays for more labour, care, and cleanliness. The dairy becomes more worthy of the farmer's attention, and the quality of its produce gradually improves. The price at last gets so high, that it becomes worth while to employ some of the most fertile and best cultivated lands in feeding cattle merely for the purpose of the dairy; and when it has got to this height, it cannot well go higher. If it did, more land would soon be turned to this purpose. It seems to have got to this height through the greater part of England, where much good land is commonly employed in this manner. If you except the neighbourhood of a few considerable towns, it seems not yet to have got to this height anywhere in Scotland, where common farmers seldom employ much good land in raising food for cattle, merely for the purpose of the dairy. The price of the produce, though it has risen very considerably within these few years, is probably still too low to admit of it. The inferiority of the quality, indeed, compared with that of the produce of English dairies, is fully equal to that of the price. But this inferiority of quality is, perhaps, rather the effect of this lowness of price, than the cause of it. Though the quality was much better, the greater part of what is brought to market could not, I apprehend, in the present circumstances of the country, be disposed of at a much better price; and the present price, it is probable, would not pay the expense of the land and labour necessary for producing a much better quality. Through the greater part of England, notwithstanding the superiority of price, the dairy is not reckoned a more profitable employment of land than the raising of corn, or the fattening of cattle, the two great objects of agriculture. Through the greater part of Scotland, therefore, it cannot yet be even so profitable.
p209.zh: 乳制品的生意,如猪和家禽的喂养,最初是作为全省而进行.养牛场生产的牛奶一定比养殖幼年或农民家庭所需的牛奶多,而且它们在特定季节生产的产品最多。 但是,在土地的所有生产中,牛奶也许是最易腐烂的。 在温暖的季节,当它最丰富的时候, 它将很少保持4到20小时。农夫们,通过将它制成新鲜的黄油,将它储存了一个星期;通过将它制成盐黄油,一年;通过将它制成奶酪,他储存了更多的一部分,几年. 其中一部分留给自己的家庭使用;其余的则去市场,以便找到应该拥有的最佳价格,而很少得到如此低的价格是阻止他将超出自己家庭使用范围的任何东西寄出去。 如果确实非常低,他很可能会以非常淫荡和肮脏的方式管理他的乳制品,而且可能很少认为在拥有一个特定的房间或为此而建造一个专门的房间的同时,这是值得的,但将会在他自己厨房的烟雾、污秽和肮脏中承受经营,就像30或40年前苏格兰几乎所有农民的乳制品一样,而且许多奶制品仍然如此。 同样的原因,也逐渐提高屠宰肉的价格,增加需求,再加上国家改善,减少可以少花钱或不花钱供养的数量,同样提高了乳制品的产量,其中价格自然地与屠宰肉类相联,或与喂牛费相合.物价的上涨为更多的劳动力、护理和清洁支付费用。奶制品更值得农民注意,其产品质量逐渐提高.价格终于如此高,因此在仅仅为了奶制品的目的而使用一些最肥沃和最优良的耕地喂牛的时候,变得如此值得;当它达到这个高度时,它再高不过了。 如果是这样的话,不久就会有更多的土地转向这个目的. 它似乎已经达到这个高度,穿过了英格兰的大部分地区,在那里很多好的土地通常以这种方式使用.苏格兰一般农民很少用好土地养牛, 只是为了奶制品。农产品的价格虽然在这几年里大幅上涨,但可能仍然太低,无法承认。 实际上,与英国乳制品相比,质量低劣完全等于价格低劣。 但质量的这种低劣或许是这种低价的影响,而不是其原因. 虽然质量好得多,但市场带来的大部分产品都无法出售,但我认为,在国家目前的情况下,可以以更好的价格处理;而目前的价格很可能不会支付生产质量好得多的土地和劳动力所需的费用。 通过英格兰的较大部分,尽管价格优越,乳制品并没有被算作比种植玉米,或养牛,这两个农业大客体更有利可图的地产就业. 因此,通过苏格兰的大部分地区,它甚至还不能如此有利可图。

p210.original: The lands of no country, it is evident, can ever be completely cultivated and improved, till once the price of every produce, which human industry is obliged to raise upon them, has got so high as to pay for the expense of complete improvement and cultivation. In order to do this, the price of each particular produce must be sufficient, first, to pay the rent of good corn land, as it is that which regulates the rent of the greater part of other cultivated land; and, secondly, to pay the labour and expense of the farmer, as well as they are commonly paid upon good corn land; or, in other words, to replace with the ordinary profits the stock which he employs about it. This rise in the price of each particular produce; must evidently be previous to the improvement and cultivation of the land which is destined for raising it. Gain is the end of all improvement; and nothing could deserve that name, of which loss was to be the necessary consequence. But loss must be the necessary consequence of improving land for the sake of a produce of which the price could never bring back the expense. If the complete improvement and cultivation of the country be, as it most certainly is, the greatest of all public advantages, this rise in the price of all those different sorts of rude produce, instead of being considered as a public calamity, ought to be regarded as the necessary forerunner and attendant of the greatest of all public advantages.
p210.zh: 显然,任何国家的土地都不可能完全耕种和改善,直到人类工业不得不向它们提高的每种产品的价格一度高到支付全部改良和种植的费用。 为了做到这一点,每种特定农产品的价格必须足以支付好玉米地的租金,因为它管制着其他大部分耕地的租金;第二,支付农民的劳力和费用,以及通常在好玉米地上支付的费用;或者,换句话说,用他所雇用的股票的普通利润来代替。每种特定产品价格的上涨,显然必须先于改良和种植准备种植的土地。增益是所有改进的结束;没有任何东西值得用这个名称,而损失是其必然后果。 但是,损失必须是改善土地的必要后果,以换取价格永远无法收回成本的农产品。 如果国家的全面改善和种植 -- -- 正如它最肯定的 -- -- 是所有公共利益中最大的,那么所有这些不同类型无礼产品价格的上涨,而不是被视为公共灾难,就应被视为所有公共利益中最伟大的先行者和伴随者。

p211.original: This rise, too, in the nominal or money price of all those different sorts of rude produce, has been the effect, not of any degradation in the value of silver, but of a rise in their real price. They have become worth, not only a greater quantity of silver, but a greater quantity of labour and subsistence than before. As it costs a greater quantity of labour and subsistence to bring them to market, so, when they are brought thither they represent, or are equivalent to a greater quantity.
p211.zh: 以上种种无礼产品的名义价格或货币价格的上涨,也产生了效果,不是银值的任何下降,而是其实际价格的上升。 它们已经变得值钱,不仅增加了白银的数量,而且比以前增加了劳动力和生计的数量.将她们带入市场需要更多的劳动力和生计,因此,当她们被带到市场上时,她们代表或相当于更多的人。

p212.original: Third Sort.--The third and last sort of rude produce, of which the price naturally rises in the progress of improvement, is that in which the efficacy of human industry, in augmenting the quantity, is either limited or uncertain. Though the real price of this sort of rude produce, therefore, naturally tends to rise in the progress of improvement, yet, according as different accidents happen to render the efforts of human industry more or less successful in augmenting the quantity, it may happen sometimes even to fall, sometimes to continue the same, in very different periods of improvement, and sometimes to rise more or less in the same period.
p212.zh: 第三类——第三类也是最后一类无礼产品,其中价格在改进过程中自然上升,就是人类工业在增加数量方面的功效是有限的,或者是不确定的。 因此,虽然这种无礼产品的实际价格自然会随着改进的进展而上升,但是,由于不同事故的发生,使人类工业的努力在增加数量方面或多或少取得成功,有时甚至会下降,有时会继续下降,在非常不同的改进时期,有时会上升。

p213.original: There are some sorts of rude produce which nature has rendered a kind of appendages to other sorts; so that the quantity of the one which any country can afford, is necessarily limited by that of the other. The quantity of wool or of raw hides, for example, which any country can afford, is necessarily limited by the number of great and small cattle that are kept in it. The state of its improvement, and the nature of its agriculture, again necessarily determine this number.
p213.zh: 有一些粗鲁的产物,大自然给其他种类的产物带来了某种附属物;因此,任何国家能够负担的产物的数量必然受到另一个国家的产物的数量的限制。 例如,任何国家都买得起的羊毛或生羊皮的数量,必然受到所保存的大牛和小牛的数量的限制。 它的改善状况和农业的性质也必然决定了这个数目。

p214.original: The same causes which, in the progress of improvement, gradually raise the price of butcher's meat, should have the same effect, it may be thought, upon the prices of wool and raw hides, and raise them, too, nearly in the same proportion. It probably would be so, if, in the rude beginnings of improvement, the market for the latter commodities was confined within as narrow bounds as that for the former. But the extent of their respective markets is commonly extremely different.
p214.zh: 在改进过程中,同样的原因,逐步提高屠夫肉的价格,应该产生同样的效果,可以认为,对羊毛和生皮的价格,也差不多一样提高. 如果在粗鲁的改进初期,后一种商品的市场被限制在与前者一样的狭小界限内,那就可能是这样了。 但是,它们各自市场的范围通常极为不同。

p215.original: The market for butcher's meat is almost everywhere confined to the country which produces it. Ireland, and some part of British America, indeed, carry on a considerable trade in salt provisions; but they are, I believe, the only countries in the commercial world which do so, or which export to other countries any considerable part of their butcher's meat.
p215.zh: 屠宰肉的市场几乎局限于生产肉类的国家。 事实上,爱尔兰和英美的一些地区进行着相当可观的盐类贸易;但我认为,它们是商业世界中唯一这样做的国家,或向其他国家出口其屠宰肉的任何相当一部分。

p216.original: The market for wool and raw hides, on the contrary, is, in the rude beginnings of improvement, very seldom confined to the country which produces them. They can easily be transported to distant countries; wool without any preparation, and raw hides with very little; and as they are the materials of many manufactures, the industry of other countries may occasion a demand for them, though that of the country which produces them might not occasion any.
p216.zh: 相反,羊毛和生皮的市场在粗鲁的改善初期,很少局限于生产羊毛和生皮的国家。 它们很容易被运往遥远的国家;毛不作任何准备,生皮很少;由于它们是许多制成品的原料,其他国家工业可能会对它们产生需求,尽管生产羊毛的国家可能不会产生任何需求。

p217.original: In countries ill cultivated, and therefore but thinly inhabited, the price of the wool and the hide bears always a much greater proportion to that of the whole beast, than in countries where, improvement and population being further advanced, there is more demand for butcher's meat. Mr Hume observes, that in the Saxon times, the fleece was estimated at two-fifths of the value of the whole sheep and that this was much above the proportion of its present estimation. In some provinces of Spain, I have been assured, the sheep is frequently killed merely for the sake of the fleece and the tallow. The carcase is often left to rot upon the ground, or to be devoured by beasts and birds of prey. If this sometimes happens even in Spain, it happens almost constantly in Chili, at Buenos Ayres, and in many other parts of Spanish America, where the horned cattle are almost constantly killed merely for the sake of the hide and the tallow. This, too, used to happen almost constantly in Hispaniola, while it was infested by the buccaneers, and before the settlement, improvement, and populousness of the French plantations ( which now extend round the coast of almost the whole western half of the island) had given some value to the cattle of the Spaniards, who still continue to possess, not only the eastern part of the coast, but the whole inland mountainous part of the country.
p217.zh: 在种植不良、因而居住稀少的国家,羊毛和皮熊的价格总是比整个野兽的价格高得多,而那些在改善和人口进一步增加的国家,对屠宰肉的需求却更大。Hume先生指出,在萨克森时代,羊群估计占整个羊群价值的五分之二,这远远高于目前估计的五分之二。 在西班牙的一些省份,我得到保证,绵羊常常仅仅因为羊群和高地而被杀害。尸体常常被留在地上腐烂,或者被猎物的野兽和鸟类吞噬. 如果这种情况有时甚至在西班牙发生,几乎经常发生在奇利,布宜诺斯艾利斯艾雷斯,以及西班牙美洲的许多其他地区,在那里,角牛几乎经常被杀,仅仅是为了躲猫猫和高地. 这在伊斯帕尼奥拉也几乎时常发生,同时它被布卡内人侵扰,在法国种植园(现在几乎整个西半岛的海岸被延伸)的定居,改良,人口众多之前,已经给西班牙人的牛提供了一定的价值,他们仍然拥有,不仅是海岸的东部,还有整个内陆山区.

p218.original: Though, in the progress of improvement and population, the price of the whole beast necessarily rises, yet the price of the carcase is likely to be much more affected by this rise than that of the wool and the hide. The market for the carcase being in the rude state of society confined always to the country which produces it, must necessarily be extended in proportion to the improvement and population of that country. But the market for the wool and the hides, even of a barbarous country, often extending to the whole commercial world, it can very seldom be enlarged in the same proportion. The state of the whole commercial world can seldom be much affected by the improvement of any particular country; and the market for such commodities may remain the same, or very nearly the same, after such improvements, as before. It should, however, in the natural course of things, rather, upon the whole, be somewhat extended in consequence of them. If the manufactures, especially, of which those commodities are the materials, should ever come to flourish in the country, the market, though it might not be much enlarged, would at least be brought much nearer to the place of growth than before; and the price of those materials might at least be increased by what had usually been the expense of transporting them to distant countries. Though it might not rise, therefore, in the same proportion as that of butcher's meat, it ought naturally to rise somewhat, and it ought certainly not to fall.
p218.zh: 虽然在改良和人口进步中,整个野兽的价格必然会上升,然而卡皮的价格受到这种上涨的影响可能远大于羊毛和藏物的价格.汽车市场处于社会无礼状态,始终局限于生产汽车的国家,必须按该国改善和人口比例予以扩大。 但羊毛和羊皮市场,即使是野蛮国家,往往扩展到整个商业世界,也很少能够以同样的比例扩大。任何特定国家的改善都很少影响整个商业世界的状况;这种商品的市场在改善后可能保持不变,或几乎保持不变。 然而,在自然过程中,总的来讲,它应在某种程度上扩大。 如果特别是这些商品作为原料的制成品在该国兴旺发展,市场虽然可能没有太大扩大,但至少会比以前更接近增长地点;这些材料的价格至少会因通常运输到遥远国家的费用而增加。 尽管它可能不会上升,因此,以与屠夫的肉一样的比例上升,但它自然应该有所上升,当然它不应该下降。

p219.original: In England, however, notwithstanding the flourishing state of its woollen manufacture, the price of English wool has fallen very considerably since the time of Edward III. There are many authentic records which demonstrate that, during the reign of that prince (towards the middle of the fourteenth century, or about 1339), what was reckoned the moderate and reasonable price of the tod, or twenty-eight pounds of English wool, was not less than ten shillings of the money of those times {See Smith's Memoirs of Wool, vol. i c. 5, 6, 7. also vol. ii.}, containing, at the rate of twenty-pence the ounce, six ounces of silver, Tower weight, equal to about thirty shillings of our present money. In the present times, one-and-twenty shillings the tod may be reckoned a good price for very good English wool. The money price of wool, therefore, in the time of Edward III. was to its money price in the present times as ten to seven. The superiority of its real price was still greater. At the rate of six shillings and eightpence the quarter, ten shillings was in those ancient times the price of twelve bushels of wheat. At the rate of twenty-eight shillings the quarter, one-and-twenty shillings is in the present times the price of six bushels only. The proportion between the real price of ancient and modern times, therefore, is as twelve to six, or as two to one. In those ancient times, a tod of wool would have purchased twice the quantity of subsistence which it will purchase at present, and consequently twice the quantity of labour, if the real recompence of labour had been the same in both periods.
p219.zh: 然而,在英国,尽管其羊毛制造的兴盛状态,英国羊毛的价格自爱德华三世时代以来已经大幅下跌.有许多真实的记录表明,在这位王子统治期间(到14世纪中叶,或约1339年),人们所估计的托德的温和合理价格,或28磅的英国羊毛,不低于那些时代钱的10先令{见史密斯的伍尔回忆录,第i卷c.5, 6, 7, 也vol.ii.},按20便士的速率, 装有6盎司的银,塔重量, 相当于我们目前钱的30先令。 在当今的时代,一二十先令的托德可能被认为是非常优秀的英国羊毛的好价钱. 因此,在爱德华三世时代,羊毛的货币价格是目前以10到7的货币价格。其实际价格的优越性仍然更大。以6先令和8便士的速率,10先令在那些古代是12毛耳小麦的价格。 按季度28先令的速度,目前只有1和20先令的价格是6毛耳。 因此,古代和现代的实际价格的比例是12比6,或者2比1. 在这些古代,如果两个时期的劳动力实际补偿相同,那么一头羊毛本来可以购买目前所购买的两倍的生计,从而购买两倍的劳动力。

p220.original: This degradation, both in the real and nominal value of wool, could never have happened in consequence of the natural course of things. It has accordingly been the effect of violence and artifice. First, of the absolute prohibition of exporting wool from England: secondly, of the permission of importing it from Spain, duty free: thirdly, of the prohibition of exporting it from Ireland to another country but England. In consequence of these regulations, the market for English wool, instead of being somewhat extended, in consequence of the improvement of England, has been confined to the home market, where the wool of several other countries is allowed to come into competition with it, and where that of Ireland is forced into competition with it. As the woollen manufactures, too, of Ireland, are fully as much discouraged as is consistent with justice and fair dealing, the Irish can work up but a smaller part of their own wool at home, and are therefore obliged to send a greater proportion of it to Great Britain, the only market they are allowed.
p220.zh: 羊毛的实际价值和名义价值的这种退化不可能因自然过程而发生。 因此,这是暴力和艺术的影响。 第一,绝对禁止从英国出口羊毛:第二,允许从西班牙进口羊毛,免税:第三,禁止从爱尔兰向另一个国家出口羊毛,但英国除外. 由于这些法规,英国羊毛市场没有被稍加扩展,而是由于英格兰的改善而被限制在本土市场,允许其他几个国家的羊毛与之竞争,爱尔兰的羊毛被迫与之竞争. 由于爱尔兰的羊毛制品也完全被劝阻,与正义和公平交易一致,爱尔兰人可以自己在家养羊,但只有一小部分羊毛,因此不得不将羊毛的更大比例送到英国,这是他们被允许的唯一市场。

p221.original: I have not been able to find any such authentic records concerning the price of raw hides in ancient times. Wool was commonly paid as a subsidy to the king, and its valuation in that subsidy ascertains, at least in some degree, what was its ordinary price. But this seems not to have been the case with raw hides. Fleetwood, however, from an account in 1425, between the prior of Burcester Oxford and one of his canons, gives us their price, at least as it was stated upon that particular occasion, viz. five ox hides at twelve shillings; five cow hides at seven shillings and threepence; thirtysix sheep skins of two years old at nine shillings; sixteen calf skins at two shillings. In 1425, twelve shillings contained about the same quantity of silver as four-and-twenty shillings of our present money. An ox hide, therefore, was in this account valued at the same quantity of silver as 4s. 4/5ths of our present money. Its nominal price was a good deal lower than at present. But at the rate of six shillings and eightpence the quarter, twelve shillings would in those times have purchased fourteen bushels and four-fifths of a bushel of wheat, which, at three and sixpence the bushel, would in the present times cost 51s. 4d. An ox hide, therefore, would in those times have purchased as much corn as ten shillings and threepence would purchase at present. Its real value was equal to ten shillings and threepence of our present money. In those ancient times, when the cattle were half starved during the greater part of the winter, we cannot suppose that they were of a very large size. An ox hide which weighs four stone of sixteen pounds of avoirdupois, is not in the present times reckoned a bad one; and in those ancient times would probably have been reckoned a very good one. But at half-a-crown the stone, which at this moment (February 1773) I understand to be the common price, such a hide would at present cost only ten shillings. Through its nominal price, therefore, is higher in the present than it was in those ancient times, its real price, the real quantity of subsistence which it will purchase or command, is rather somewhat lower. The price of cow hides, as stated in the above account, is nearly in the common proportion to that of ox hides. That of sheep skins is a good deal above it. They had probably been sold with the wool. That of calves skins, on the contrary, is greatly below it. In countries where the price of cattle is very low, the calves, which are not intended to be reared in order to keep up the stock, are generally killed very young, as was the case in Scotland twenty or thirty years ago. It saves the milk, which their price would not pay for. Their skins, therefore, are commonly good for little.
p221.zh: 我无法找到任何关于古代生化藏品价格的这种真实记录。伍尔通常作为给国王的补贴而支付,其在该补贴中的估值至少在某种程度上可以确定它的一般价格是什么. 但原始的藏品似乎并非如此。 然而,Fleetwood在1425年的一个账户中,在布尔塞斯特牛津的前身和他的一个罐头之间,至少按照当时的说法,给我们定价,即5头牛藏在12先令处;5头牛藏在7先令和3便士处;36头羊皮2岁,9先令处;16头牛皮藏在2先令处。 在1425年,12先令 包含大约相同的银数量 与我们目前钱的4和20先令。 因此,这一账户中藏有一只牛,其价值与4银相同。 我们现款的四分之一其名义价格比目前低了很多。 但以6先令和8便士的汇率计算,12先令在那些时候会购买14毛耳和5毛耳的小麦,在目前时间里,以3和6便士的毛耳将花费51美元。4d. (中文(简体) ). 因此,在那些时候,一头牛会购买多达10先令和3便士的玉米。其实际价值相当于我们现今钱的十先令和三便士。 在那些古老的时代,当在大半个冬天里,牛被饿得半死的时候,我们不能想象它们大小很大.一只公牛藏着16磅重的牛,在当今时代并不认为是坏的;在那些古代,很可能被认为是非常好的。 但是在半裸的石头上, 此时此刻(1773年2月)我明白这是共同的代价, 这样的藏物现在只花费十先令。 因此,通过其名义价格,目前的价格比那些古代的价格要高,其实际价格,即它将购买或购买的维持生计的实际数量,略低一些。牛皮价格,如上所述,与牛皮价格几乎成同比例.羊皮的这个是上好的交易很可能是用羊毛卖的幼崽的皮肤,恰恰相反, 远远低于它。 在牛价非常低的国家,小牛一般都是很年轻被杀的,二,三十年前苏格兰就是这种情况,这些小牛不是为了养活牲畜而准备复活的.它可以节省牛奶,而他们的价格是无法支付的。 因此,它们的皮肤通常对很少有好处。

p222.original: The price of raw hides is a good deal lower at present than it was a few years ago; owing probably to the taking off the duty upon seal skins, and to the allowing, for a limited time, the importation of raw hides from Ireland, and from the plantations, duty free, which was done in 1769. Take the whole of the present century at an average, their real price has probably been somewhat higher than it was in those ancient times. The nature of the commodity renders it not quite so proper for being transported to distant markets as wool. It suffers more by keeping. A salted hide is reckoned inferior to a fresh one, and sells for a lower price. This circumstance must necessarily have some tendency to sink the price of raw hides produced in a country which does not manufacture them, but is obliged to export them, and comparatively to raise that of those produced in a country which does manufacture them. It must have some tendency to sink their price in a barbarous, and to raise it in an improved and manufacturing country. It must have had some tendency, therefore, to sink it in ancient, and to raise it in modern times. Our tanners, besides, have not been quite so successful as our clothiers, in convincing the wisdom of the nation, that the safety of the commonwealth depends upon the prosperity of their particular manufacture. They have accordingly been much less favoured. The exportation of raw hides has, indeed, been prohibited, and declared a nuisance; but their importation from foreign countries has been subjected to a duty; and though this duty has been taken off from those of Ireland and the plantations (for the limited time of five years only), yet Ireland has not been confined to the market of Great Britain for the sale of its surplus hides, or of those which are not manufactured at home. The hides of common cattle have, but within these few years, been put among the enumerated commodities which the plantations can send nowhere but to the mother country; neither has the commerce of Ireland been in this case oppressed hitherto, in order to support the manufactures of Great Britain.
p222.zh: 原藏品的价格比现在的几年前低了很多;这可能是由于在海豹皮上卸下关税,以及允许在有限的时间内从爱尔兰进口原藏品,以及从种植园进口免关税的原藏品,这在1769年完成. 从整个本世纪的平均值来看,它们的实际价格可能比那些古老时代要高一些。 由于商品的性质,将羊毛运输到遥远的市场并不十分合适。 它承受更多的痛苦 通过保持。咸藏被算作劣于鲜藏,以低价出售. 这种情况必然有某种倾向,使不生产这种产品的国家生产的原藏品的价格下降,但必须出口这种产品,相对而言,必须提高生产这种产品的国家的原藏品的价格。 它一定有某种倾向,在野蛮中降低价格,在一个改良和制造的国家中提高价格。 因此,它一定有某种倾向,在古代沉没,在现代饲养. 此外,我们的制革厂没有像我们的布衣厂家那样成功地说服全国的智慧,即联邦的安全取决于其特定制造的繁荣。 因此,它们得到的青睐要少得多。 事实上,原藏品出口是被禁止的,并被宣布为有害物;但从外国进口原藏品是必须履行的一项义务;虽然该义务是从爱尔兰和种植园的原藏品出口的(仅限5年时间),但爱尔兰并未被限制在大不列颠市场出售其剩余藏品,或出售未在本国制造的藏品。通常的牛皮在过去几年中被放在列举的商品中,种植园只能向祖国寄送这些商品;在这种情况下,爱尔兰的商业也从未受到压迫,以支持大不列颠的制造业。

p223.original: Whatever regulations tend to sink the price, either of wool or of raw hides, below what it naturally would he, must, in an improved and cultivated country, have some tendency to raise the price of butcher's meat. The price both of the great and small cattle, which are fed on improved and cultivated land, must be sufficient to pay the rent which the landlord, and the profit which the farmer, has reason to expect from improved and cultivated land. If it is not, they will soon cease to feed them. Whatever part of this price, therefore, is not paid by the wool and the hide, must be paid by the carcase. The less there is paid for the one, the more must be paid for the other. In what manner this price is to be divided upon the different parts of the beast, is indifferent to the landlords and farmers, provided it is all paid to them. In an improved and cultivated country, therefore, their interest as landlords and farmers cannot be much affected by such regulations, though their interest as consumers may, by the rise in the price of provisions. It would be quite otherwise, however, in an unimproved and uncultivated country, where the greater part of the lands could be applied to no other purpose but the feeding of cattle, and where the wool and the hide made the principal part of the value of those cattle. Their interest as landlords and farmers would in this case be very deeply affected by such regulations, and their interest as consumers very little. The fall in the price of the wool and the hide would not in this case raise the price of the carcase; because the greater part of the lands of the country being applicable to no other purpose but the feeding of cattle, the same number would still continue to be fed. The same quantity of butcher's meat would still come to market. The demand for it would be no greater than before. Its price, therefore, would be the same as before. The whole price of cattle would fall, and along with it both the rent and the profit of all those lands of which cattle was the principal produce, that is, of the greater part of the lands of the country. The perpetual prohibition of the exportation of wool, which is commonly, but very falsely, ascribed to Edward III., would, in the then circumstances of the country, have been the most destructive regulation which could well have been thought of. It would not only have reduced the actual value of the greater part of the lands in the kingdom, but by reducing the price of the most important species of small cattle, it would have retarded very much its subsequent improvement.
p223.zh: 无论什么规定,无论是羊毛还是生皮,其价格都低于他自然会的价格,在一个改良和种植的国家,必须具有某种提高屠夫肉价格的趋势。以改良和耕地为食的大牛和小牛的价格必须足以支付地主的租金,以及农民有理由期望从改良和耕地中获得的利润。 如果不是,他们很快就会停止养活他们。 因此,无论这部分价格是多少,羊毛和皮毛都不用支付,都必须用车厢支付。 一者所得少者,必得多者. 这种价钱如何分给野兽的不同部位,对地主和农民漠不关心,只要全部都付给他们. 因此,在一个改良和种植的国家,他们作为地主和农民的利益不会受到这种条例的很大影响,尽管他们作为消费者的利益可能受到供应价格上升的影响。 然而,在一个未经改良和未开垦的国家,土地的大部分只能用于喂养牛,羊毛和羊皮是这些牛的主要价值。 在这种情况下,他们作为地主和农民的利益将受到这种条例的严重影响,他们作为消费者的利益很小。羊毛和藏物价格的下跌在此情况下不会提高卡具的价格;因为该国大部分土地除了喂养牛之外没有其他用途,同样数量的土地仍然会继续被喂食.同样的肉类数量 仍然会上市。 对它的要求不会比以前更大。 因此,其价格将同以前一样。牛的整个价格将下降,与此同时,所有以牛为主要产品的土地的租金和利润,即该国大部分土地的租金和利润都将下降。永远禁止出口羊毛 -- -- 通常但非常错误地归咎于爱德华三世 -- -- 在当时的国情中,这本来是最具有破坏性的规章,人们完全可以想到。 它不仅会降低王国中大部分土地的实际价值,而且通过降低最重要的小牛品种的价格,会大大减慢后来的改良.

p224.original: The wool of Scotland fell very considerably in its price in consequence of the union with England, by which it was excluded from the great market of Europe, and confined to the narrow one of Great Britain. The value of the greater part of the lands in the southern counties of Scotland, which are chiefly a sheep country, would have been very deeply affected by this event, had not the rise in the price of butcher's meat fully compensated the fall in the price of wool.
p224.zh: 苏格兰的羊毛由于与英格兰的结合而价格大幅下跌,因为英格兰被排斥在欧洲的大市场之外,并局限于大不列颠的狭义市场.苏格兰南部各郡大部分土地主要是羊国,如果屠夫肉价格的上涨没有完全补偿羊毛价格的下跌,那么这些土地的价值就会受到这一事件的非常深刻的影响.

p225.original: As the efficacy of human industry, in increasing the quantity either of wool or of raw hides, is limited, so far as it depends upon the produce of the country where it is exerted; so it is uncertain so far as it depends upon the produce of other countries. It so far depends not so much upon the quantity which they produce, as upon that which they do not manufacture; and upon the restraints which they may or may not think proper to impose upon the exportation of this sort of rude produce. These circumstances, as they are altogether independent of domestic industry, so they necessarily render the efficacy of its efforts more or less uncertain. In multiplying this sort of rude produce, therefore, the efficacy of human industry is not only limited, but uncertain.
p225.zh: 由于人类工业在增加羊毛或生皮数量方面的功效有限,因为它取决于所产国家的产品;因此,它取决于其他国家的产品,因此是不确定的。 迄今为止,这与其说取决于它们生产的数量,不如说取决于它们不生产的数量;还取决于它们可能认为或可能认为不适宜对出口这种无礼产品施加的限制。这些情况完全独立于国内工业,因此,它们必然使其努力的效力多少不确定。 因此,在将这种粗鲁的产物成倍增加时,人类工业的功效不仅有限,而且不确定。

p226.original: In multiplying another very important sort of rude produce, the quantity of fish that is brought to market, it is likewise both limited and uncertain. It is limited by the local situation of the country, by the proximity or distance of its different provinces from the sea, by the number of its lakes and rivers, and by what may be called the fertility or barrenness of those seas, lakes, and rivers, as to this sort of rude produce. As population increases, as the annual produce of the land and labour of the country grows greater and greater, there come to be more buyers of fish; and those buyers, too, have a greater quantity and variety of other goods, or, what is the same thing, the price of a greater quantity and variety of other goods, to buy with. But it will generally be impossible to supply the great and extended market, without employing a quantity of labour greater than in proportion to what had been requisite for supplying the narrow and confined one. A market which, from requiring only one thousand, comes to require annually ten thousand ton of fish, can seldom be supplied, without employing more than ten times the quantity of labour which had before been sufficient to supply it. The fish must generally be sought for at a greater distance, larger vessels must be employed, and more expensive machinery of every kind made use of. The real price of this commodity, therefore, naturally rises in the progress of improvement. It has accordingly done so, I believe, more or less in every country.
p226.zh: 将另一种非常重要的粗鲁产品,即上市的鱼的数量,加以乘以,同样是有限的,也是不确定的。受国家当地情况,不同省份与海洋相近或相距遥远,湖泊和河流数量,以及这些海洋、湖泊和河流的肥力或贫瘠程度的限制,这种无礼的产物是有限的。 随着人口的增长,随着全国土地年产量和劳动力的不断增长,鱼类的购买者也越来越多;这些购买者也拥有数量和种类较多的其他商品,或者说,同样的事情,是购买数量和种类较多的其他商品的价格。 但是,如果不雇用比供应狭窄和封闭的市场所需数量更多的劳动力,一般不可能供应大而扩大的市场。市场每年需要1 000吨鱼,但很少能够供应,而且不能雇用比以前足够供应的劳动力多十倍以上的劳动力。通常必须更远地寻找这些鱼,必须使用更大的船只,以及使用各种昂贵的机器。 因此,这种商品的实际价格自然会随着改进的进展而上升。 我认为,它已经在每个国家大致如此。

p227.original: Though the success of a particular day's fishing maybe a very uncertain matter, yet the local situation of the country being supposed, the general efficacy of industry in bringing a certain quantity of fish to market, taking the course of a year, or of several years together, it may, perhaps, be thought is certain enough; and it, no doubt, is so. As it depends more, however, upon the local situation of the country, than upon the state of its wealth and industry; as upon this account it may in different countries be the same in very different periods of improvement, and very different in the same period; its connection with the state of improvement is uncertain; and it is of this sort of uncertainty that I am here speaking.
p227.zh: 虽然某一天的捕鱼活动的成功也许是一个非常不确定的问题,然而,应该从该国的地方情况来看,工业将一定数量的鱼投入市场、经过一年或几年的时间,其总的功效或许可以认为已经足够确定;毫无疑问,工业是完全确定的。 然而,这更多地取决于该国的地方情况,而不是其财富和工业的状况;就这一点而言,在不同国家,在非常不同的改进时期,它可能是一样的,在同一时期则完全不同;它与改进状况的关系是不确定的;我在这里发言的正是这种不确定性。

p228.original: In increasing the quantity of the different minerals and metals which are drawn from the bowels of the earth, that of the more precious ones particularly, the efficacy of human industry seems not to be limited, but to be altogether uncertain.
p228.zh: 在增加从地肠中提取的不同矿物和金属的数量,特别是较珍贵的矿物和金属的数量方面,人类工业的功效似乎不是有限的,而是完全不确定的。

p229.original: The quantity of the precious metals which is to be found in any country, is not limited by any thing in its local situation, such as the fertility or barrenness of its own mines. Those metals frequently abound in countries which possess no mines. Their quantity, in every particular country, seems to depend upon two different circumstances; first, upon its power of purchasing, upon the state of its industry, upon the annual produce of its land and labour, in consequence of which it can afford to employ a greater or a smaller quantity of labour and subsistence, in bringing or purchasing such superfluities as gold and silver, either from its own mines, or from those of other countries; and, secondly, upon the fertility or barrenness of the mines which may happen at any particular time to supply the commercial world with those metals. The quantity of those metals in the countries most remote from the mines, must be more or less affected by this fertility or barrenness, on account of the easy and cheap transportation of those metals, of their small bulk and great value. Their quantity in China and Indostan must have been more or less affected by the abundance of the mines of America.
p229.zh: 任何国家都能找到的贵金属数量不受本国情况的任何限制,例如本国矿山的肥力或贫瘠程度。 这些金属在无矿的国家中经常大量存在。在每个特定国家,其数量似乎取决于两种不同的情况:第一,取决于其购买能力,取决于其工业状况,取决于其土地和劳动力的年度产量,因此,它能够雇用更多或更少的劳动力和生计,从自己的矿山或从其他国家矿山购买黄金和白银等超流物;第二,取决于矿山的肥力或贫瘠程度,这些矿山可能在任何特定时间向商业世界供应这些金属。 在离矿山最远的国家,这些金属的数量必须多少受到这种肥力或贫瘠的影响,因为这些金属的运输既方便又便宜,其散装量小,价值巨大。在中国和印度斯坦,其数量一定多少受到美国地雷丰度的影响。

p230.original: So far as their quantity in any particular country depends upon the former of those two circumstances (the power of purchasing), their real price, like that of all other luxuries and superfluities, is likely to rise with the wealth and improvement of the country, and to fall with its poverty and depression. Countries which have a great quantity of labour and subsistence to spare, can afford to purchase any particular quantity of those metals at the expense of a greater quantity of labour and subsistence, than countries which have less to spare.
p230.zh: 其数量在任何特定国家都取决于这两种情况(购买力)中的前一种情况,其实际价格,如所有其他奢侈品和超级奢侈品的价格,随着国家的财富和改善,有可能上升,并随着国家的贫穷和萧条而下降。拥有大量剩余劳动力和生计的国家,比那些没有足够余力的国家更有能力以牺牲更多劳动力和生计为代价购买任何特定数量的金属。

p231.original: So far as their quantity in any particular country depends upon the latter of those two circumstances (the fertility or barrenness of the mines which happen to supply the commercial world), their real price, the real quantity of labour and subsistence which they will purchase or exchange for, will, no doubt, sink more or less in proportion to the fertility, and rise in proportion to the barrenness of those mines.
p231.zh: 只要在任何特定国家中,其数量取决于这两种情况中的后一种情况(为商业世界供应的矿井的肥力或贫力)、其实际价格、它们将购买或交换的劳动力和生计的实际数量,无疑将多少与肥力成比例地下降,并随着这些矿井贫瘠程度的上升而上升。

p232.original: The fertility or barrenness of the mines, however, which may happen at any particular time to supply the commercial world, is a circumstance which, it is evident, may have no sort of connection with the state of industry in a particular country. It seems even to have no very necessary connection with that of the world in general. As arts and commerce, indeed, gradually spread themselves over a greater and a greater part of the earth, the search for new mines, being extended over a wider surface, may have somewhat a better chance for being successful than when confined within narrower bounds. The discovery of new mines, however, as the old ones come to be gradually exhausted, is a matter of the greatest uncertainty, and such as no human skill or industry can insure. All indications, it is acknowledged, are doubtful; and the actual discovery and successful working of a new mine can alone ascertain the reality of its value, or even of its existence. In this search there seem to be no certain limits, either to the possible success, or to the possible disappointment of human industry. In the course of a century or two, it is possible that new mines may be discovered, more fertile than any that have ever yet been known; and it is just equally possible, that the most fertile mine then known may be more barren than any that was wrought before the discovery of the mines of America. Whether the one or the other of those two events may happen to take place, is of very little importance to the real wealth and prosperity of the world, to the real value of the annual produce of the land and labour of mankind. Its nominal value, the quantity of gold and silver by which this annual produce could be expressed or represented, would, no doubt, be very different; but its real value, the real quantity of labour which it could purchase or command, would be precisely the same. A shilling might, in the one case, represent no more labour than a penny does at present; and a penny, in the other, might represent as much as a shilling does now. But in the one case, he who had a shilling in his pocket would be no richer than he who has a penny at present; and in the other, he who had a penny would be just as rich as he who has a shilling now. The cheapness and abundance of gold and silver plate would be the sole advantage which the world could derive from the one event; and the dearness and scarcity of those trifling superfluities, the only inconveniency it could suffer from the other.
p232.zh: 然而,矿山的肥力或贫瘠程度,在任何特定时间都可能发生,以便为商业世界提供供应,这种情况显然与某一特定国家的工业状况没有某种联系。 它甚至似乎与整个世界的这种联系并不十分必要。 事实上,随着艺术和商业逐渐蔓延到地球上更大和更大的地方,寻找新的地雷,在更大的地表上扩展,比在狭窄的界限内寻找地雷,有更好的成功机会。 然而,随着旧地雷逐渐耗尽,发现新地雷是一个最不确定的问题,例如,任何人类技能或工业都无法保证。 人们承认,所有迹象都令人怀疑;而新地雷的实际发现和成功运作,只能确定它的价值,甚至其存在的真实性。 在这种探索中,似乎没有限制,无论是对可能的成功,还是对人类工业可能失望,都没有限制。 在一、两个世纪中,有可能发现新的地雷,比任何已知的更肥沃;同样可能的是,当时已知的最肥沃的地雷可能比发现美国地雷之前制造的更不育。不论这两个事件之一是否发生,对于世界的实际财富和繁荣,对于人类的土地和劳动力年产的实际价值,都没有什么意义。其名义价值,即年度产品能够表示或表示的金银数量,无疑将有很大不同;但其实际价值,即它能够购买或指挥的劳动力的实际数量,则完全相同. 在一种情况下,先令可能只是目前一分钱的劳动;而在另一种情况下,一分钱可能相当于现在一分钱的劳动。 但是,在一种情况下,口袋里有先令的人,不会比现在有一分钱的人更富;在另一种情况下,有一分钱的人,会像现在有先令的人一样富足. 金银板的廉价和丰盛将是世界唯一能够从这一事件中获得的优势;这些微弱的超级流体的匮乏和稀缺,是它唯一可能从另一个事件中遭受的不便。

p233.original: Conclusion of the Digression concerning the Variations in the Value of Silver.
p233.zh: 关于银币价值变动的变动的结论。

p234.original: The greater part of the writers who have collected the money price of things in ancient times, seem to have considered the low money price of corn, and of goods in general, or, in other words, the high value of gold and silver, as a proof, not only of the scarcity of those metals, but of the poverty and barbarism of the country at the time when it took place. This notion is connected with the system of political economy, which represents national wealth as consisting in the abundance and national poverty in the scarcity, of gold and silver; a system which I shall endeavour to explain and examine at great length in the fourth book of this Inquiry. I shall only observe at present, that the high value of the precious metals can be no proof of the poverty or barbarism of any particular country at the time when it took place. It is a proof only of the barrenness of the mines which happened at that time to supply the commercial world. A poor country, as it cannot afford to buy more, so it can as little afford to pay dearer for gold and silver than a rich one; and the value of those metals, therefore, is not likely to be higher in the former than in the latter. In China, a country much richer than any part of Europe, the value of the precious metals is much higher than in any part of Europe. As the wealth of Europe, indeed, has increased greatly since the discovery of the mines of America, so the value of gold and silver has gradually diminished. This diminution of their value, however, has not been owing to the increase of the real wealth of Europe, of the annual produce of its land and labour, but to the accidental discovery of more abundant mines than any that were known before. The increase of the quantity of gold and silver in Europe, and the increase of its manufactures and agriculture, are two events which, though they have happened nearly about the same time, yet have arisen from very different causes, and have scarce any natural connection with one another. The one has arisen from a mere accident, in which neither prudence nor policy either had or could have any share; the other, from the fall of the feudal system, and from the establishment of a government which afforded to industry the only encouragement which it requires, some tolerable security that it shall enjoy the fruits of its own labour. Poland, where the feudal system still continues to take place, is at this day as beggarly a country as it was before the discovery of America. The money price of corn, however, has risen; the real value of the precious metals has fallen in Poland, in the same manner as in other parts of Europe. Their quantity, therefore, must have increased there as in other places, and nearly in the same proportion to the annual produce of its land and labour. This increase of the quantity of those metals, however, has not, it seems, increased that annual produce, has neither improved the manufactures and agriculture of the country, nor mended the circumstances of its inhabitants. Spain and Portugal, the countries which possess the mines, are, after Poland, perhaps the two most beggarly countries in Europe. The value of the precious metals, however, must be lower in Spain and Portugal than in any other part of Europe, as they come from those countries to all other parts of Europe, loaded, not only with a freight and an insurance, but with the expense of smuggling, their exportation being either prohibited or subjected to a duty. In proportion to the annual produce of the land and labour, therefore, their quantity must be greater in those countries than in any other part of Europe; those countries, however, are poorer than the greater part of Europe. Though the feudal system has been abolished in Spain and Portugal, it has not been succeeded by a much better.
p234.zh: 在古代收集物价的作家中,有较大一部分似乎认为玉米和一般商品的低价钱,或者说黄金和白银的高价钱,作为证明,不仅证明这些金属的稀缺性,而且证明当时国家的贫困和野蛮.这一概念与政治经济制度有关,政治经济制度代表着国家财富,即金银稀缺、全国贫穷;我将努力在本调查第四本书中详细解释和审查这一制度。 我目前只能指出,贵金属的高价值不能证明发生时任何一个国家的贫穷或野蛮行为。 这仅仅是当时为商业世界供应的矿井贫瘠的证明。穷国买不起更多的钱,因此,它付得起的黄金和白银比富翁多;因此,这些金属的价值在前者不可能高于后者。在中国这个比欧洲任何地区都富裕得多的国家,贵金属的价值远高于欧洲任何地区. 随着欧洲财富的确是,自美国矿山发现以来,金银的价值就大大增加了,因此金银的价值逐渐下降. 然而,其价值的减少并非由于欧洲的实际财富、其土地和劳动力的年产量的增加,而是由于偶然发现的矿山比以前任何已知的矿山都多。 欧洲金银数量的增加及其制造和农业的增加,是两件事情,虽然几乎是在同一时间发生的,但起因却大不相同,彼此之间几乎没有任何自然联系。其原因只有一个,既非谨慎,也非政策所为;其次,由于封建制度的垮台,以及政府成立,向工业提供了它所需要的唯一鼓励,一些可以容忍的保障,即工业将享受其劳动的成果。 波兰,封建制度至今仍在实行,今天如同发现美国之前一样,是一个乞丐国家. 然而,玉米的货币价格已经上涨;贵金属的实际价值在波兰已经下降,与欧洲其他地区一样。 因此,他们的数量必须在那里与其他地方一样增加,几乎与土地和劳动力的年产量成比例。 然而,这些金属数量的增加似乎并没有增加年产量,也没有改善该国的制造业和农业,也没有改善该国居民的情况。拥有地雷的西班牙和葡萄牙,在波兰之后,也许是欧洲最乞丐的两个国家。 然而,贵金属的价值在西班牙和葡萄牙必须低于欧洲任何其他地区,因为它们从这些国家运至欧洲所有其他地区,不仅装载货物和保险,而且包括走私的费用,其出口要么被禁止,要么必须承担义务。 因此,根据土地和劳动力年产量的比例,这些国家的数量必须比欧洲任何其他地区都多;然而,这些国家比欧洲大部分地区更贫穷。 虽然封建制度在西班牙和葡萄牙被废除,但并没有得到更好的成功.

p235.original: As the low value of gold and silver, therefore, is no proof of the wealth and flourishing state of the country where it takes place; so neither is their high value, or the low money price either of goods in general, or of corn in particular, any proof of its poverty and barbarism.
p235.zh: 因此,金银价值低并不能证明所处国家的财富和繁荣状态;其价值高,或一般商品、特别是玉米的低钱价格,也不能证明该国贫穷和野蛮。

p236.original: But though the low money price, either of goods in general, or of corn in particular, be no proof of the poverty or barbarism of the times, the low money price of some particular sorts of goods, such as cattle, poultry, game of all kinds, etc. in proportion to that of corn, is a most decisive one. It clearly demonstrates, first, their great abundance in proportion to that of corn, and, consequently, the great extent of the land which they occupied in proportion to what was occupied by corn; and, secondly, the low value of this land in proportion to that of corn land, and, consequently, the uncultivated and unimproved state of the far greater part of the lands of the country. It clearly demonstrates, that the stock and population of the country did not bear the same proportion to the extent of its territory, which they commonly do in civilized countries; and that society was at that time, and in that country, but in its infancy. From the high or low money price, either of goods in general, or of corn in particular, we can infer only, that the mines, which at that time happened to supply the commercial world with gold and silver, were fertile or barren, not that the country was rich or poor. But from the high or low money price of some sorts of goods in proportion to that of others, we can infer, with a degree of probability that approaches almost to certainty, that it was rich or poor, that the greater part of its lands were improved or unimproved, and that it was either in a more or less barbarous state, or in a more or less civilized one.
p236.zh: 但是,虽然一般商品,特别是玉米的低钱价格并不能证明当时的贫困或野蛮,但某些特定种类商品的低钱价格,如牛,家禽,各类游戏等,与玉米成比例,却是最决定性的. 首先,它清楚地表明,它们与玉米成比例的丰度很大,因此,它们占有的土地与玉米所占土地成比例的很大面积;其次,这种土地与玉米土地成比例的低价值,因此,该国大片土地的未耕作和未改良状态。 它清楚地表明,国家的种群和人口与其领土范围的比例不同,它们通常在文明国家中这样做;社会当时是,在那个国家,而是在它的最初阶段。 从一般商品,或特别是玉米的高价或低价,我们只能推断,当时恰巧向商业世界供应金银的矿井是肥沃或贫瘠的,而不是国家富贫. 但是,从某种商品与其它商品成比例的高价或低价来看,我们可以推断,在某种程度上,它几乎接近确定性,它富足或贫穷,其大部分土地得到改善或没有改善,或者处于或多或少野蛮的状态,或者在或多或少文明的状态.

p237.original: Any rise in the money price of goods which proceeded altogether from the degradation of the value of silver, would affect all sorts of goods equally, and raise their price universally, a third, or a fourth, or a fifth part higher, according as silver happened to lose a third, or a fourth, or a fifth part of its former value. But the rise in the price of provisions, which has been the subject of so much reasoning and conversation, does not affect all sorts of provisions equally. Taking the course of the present century at an average, the price of corn, it is acknowledged, even by those who account for this rise by the degradation of the value of silver, has risen much less than that of some other sorts of provisions. The rise in the price of those other sorts of provisions, therefore, cannot be owing altogether to the degradation of the value of silver. Some other causes must be taken into the account; and those which have been above assigned, will, perhaps, without having recourse to the supposed degradation of the value of silver, sufficiently explain this rise in those particular sorts of provisions, of which the price has actually risen in proportion to that of corn.
p237.zh: 任何货物货币价格的上涨,如果完全从银价的下降中产生,都会对各种货物产生同等影响,并且普遍提高价格,即三分之一或四分之一,或五分之一以上,因为白银碰巧损失了三分之一、四分之一或五分之一的原价值。 但是,条款价格的上涨,一直是许多推理和谈话的主题,并没有平等地影响所有种类的条款。以本世纪的平均价格,即玉米的价格来看,人们承认,即使那些由于银的贬值而导致这一上涨的人也承认,其上涨幅度远远低于某些其他种类的供给。 因此,不能完全因为白银价值的下降而造成这些其他种类供应品的价格上涨。还必须考虑到其他一些原因;上面所分配的原因也许不会涉及所谓白银价值的下降,而是充分解释这种上涨在这些特定种类的供给中的原因,其中的价格实际上已经按照玉米价格的比例上升。

p238.original: As to the price of corn itself, it has, during the sixty-four first years of the present century, and before the late extraordinary course of bad seasons, been somewhat lower than it was during the sixty-four last years of the preceding century. This fact is attested, not only by the accounts of Windsor market, but by the public fiars of all the different counties of Scotland, and by the accounts of several different markets in France, which have been collected with great diligence and fidelity by Mr Messance, and by Mr Dupré de St Maur. The evidence is more complete than could well have been expected in a matter which is naturally so very difficult to be ascertained.
p238.zh: 至于玉米本身的价格,在本世纪的头64年,在季节不景气的后期前期,玉米的价格比上世纪的最后64年略低。这一事实不仅得到了温莎市场账户的证实,而且得到了苏格兰所有不同郡的公共分界线的证实,也得到了梅桑斯先生和杜普雷·德圣毛尔先生认真和忠实地收集的法国若干不同市场的账户的证实。在一个自然非常难以查明的问题上,证据比预期的要完整。

p239.original: As to the high price of corn during these last ten or twelve years, it can be sufficiently accounted for from the badness of the seasons, without supposing any degradation in the value of silver.
p239.zh: 至于过去10年或12年玉米的高价,可以从季节的恶劣状况中充分计算出来,而不假定白银的价值有任何退化。

p240.original: The opinion, therefore, that silver is continually sinking in its value, seems not to be founded upon any good observations, either upon the prices of corn, or upon those of other provisions.
p240.zh: 因此,认为白银的价值持续下降,似乎不是建立在任何良好的观察基础上的,无论是玉米的价格,还是其他物品的价格。

p241.original: The same quantity of silver, it may perhaps be said, will, in the present times, even according to the account which has been here given, purchase a much smaller quantity of several sorts of provisions than it would have done during some part of the last century; and to ascertain whether this change be owing to a rise in the value of those goods, or to a fall in the value of silver, is only to establish a vain and useless distinction, which can be of no sort of service to the man who has only a certain quantity of silver to go to market with, or a certain fixed revenue in money. I certainly do not pretend that the knowledge of this distinction will enable him to buy cheaper. It may not, however, upon that account be altogether useless.
p241.zh: 也许可以说,同样数量的白银,在目前时代,即使根据这里的帐户,也会比上个世纪的某个时候购买数量少得多的几种供给;并且为了确定这种改变是由于这些商品的价值上升,还是由于白银的价值下降,只是建立徒劳无益的区别,这对只有一定数量的白银可以与他一起上市的人来说是没有任何好处的,还是有一定固定的金钱收入. 我当然不会假装知道这种区别将使他买得起更便宜的东西。 然而,从这一点来看,它可能并非完全无用。

p242.original: It may be of some use to the public, by affording an easy proof of the prosperous condition of the country. If the rise in the price of some sorts of provisions be owing altogether to a fall in the value of silver, it is owing to a circumstance, from which nothing can be inferred but the fertility of the American mines. The real wealth of the country, the annual produce of its land and labour, may, notwithstanding this circumstance, be either gradually declining, as in Portugal and Poland; or gradually advancing, as in most other parts of Europe. But if this rise in the price of some sorts of provisions be owing to a rise in the real value of the land which produces them, to its increased fertility, or, in consequence of more extended improvement and good cultivation, to its having been rendered fit for producing corn; it is owing to a circumstance which indicates, in the clearest manner, the prosperous and advancing state of the country. The land constitutes by far the greatest, the most important, and the most durable part of the wealth of every extensive country. It may surely be of some use, or, at least, it may give some satisfaction to the public, to have so decisive a proof of the increasing value of by far the greatest, the most important, and the most durable part of its wealth.
p242.zh: 它对公众可能有些用处,因为它提供了该国繁荣条件的简单证据。 如果说某些规定价格的上涨完全是由于白银价值的下降,那是因为某种情况,从中只能推断出美国矿山的肥力。国家的实际财富、其土地和劳动力的年产量,尽管如此,可能象葡萄牙和波兰那样,逐步下降;或者象欧洲大多数其他地区一样,逐步上升。 但是,如果某种供应品价格的上涨是由于生产这些作物的土地的实际价值上升,其肥力增加,或者由于更长期的改良和良种,其价格已经适合生产玉米;这是由于一种情况,它以最明确的方式表明该国繁荣和进步的状况。这片土地是每个广大国家财富中最伟大、最重要和最持久的一部分。肯定有一定用处,或者至少可以给公众一些满意,这样就能够决定性地证明迄今为止最伟大、最重要和最持久部分财富的价值在增加。

p243.original: It may, too, be of some use to the public, in regulating the pecuniary reward of some of its inferior servants. If this rise in the price of some sorts of provisions be owing to a fall in the value of silver, their pecuniary reward, provided it was not too large before, ought certainly to be augmented in proportion to the extent of this fall. If it is not augmented, their real recompence will evidently be so much diminished. But if this rise of price is owing to the increased value, in consequence of the improved fertility of the land which produces such provisions, it becomes a much nicer matter to judge, either in what proportion any pecuniary reward ought to be augmented, or whether it ought to be augmented at all. The extension of improvement and cultivation, as it necessarily raises more or less, in proportion to the price of corn, that of every sort of animal food, so it as necessarily lowers that of, I believe, every sort of vegetable food. It raises the price of animal food; because a great part of the land which produces it, being rendered fit for producing corn, must afford to the landlord anti farmer the rent and profit of corn land. It lowers the price of vegetable food; because, by increasing the fertility of the land, it increases its abundance. The improvements of agriculture, too, introduce many sorts of vegetable food, which requiring less land, and not more labour than corn, come much cheaper to market. Such are potatoes and maize, or what is called Indian corn, the two most important improvements which the agriculture of Europe, perhaps, which Europe itself, has received from the great extension of its commerce and navigation. Many sorts of vegetable food, besides, which in the rude state of agriculture are confined to the kitchen-garden, and raised only by the spade, come, in its improved state, to be introduced into common fields, and to be raised by the plough; such as turnips, carrots, cabbages, etc. If, in the progress of improvement, therefore, the real price of one species of food necessarily rises, that of another as necessarily falls; and it becomes a matter of more nicety to judge how far the rise in the one may be compensated by the fall in the other. When the real price of butcher's meat has once got to its height (which, with regard to every sort, except perhaps that of hogs flesh, it seems to have done through a great part of England more than a century ago), any rise which can afterwards happen in that of any other sort of animal food, cannot much affect the circumstances of the inferior ranks of people. The circumstances of the poor, through a great part of England, cannot surely be so much distressed by any rise in the price of poultry, fish, wild-fowl, or venison, as they must be relieved by the fall in that of potatoes.
p243.zh: 在管理其一些低级仆人的金钱报酬方面,它也可能对公众有所帮助。 如果某些规定价格的上涨是由于白银价值的下降,那么他们的金钱报酬,如果以前不是太大,当然应该按照这一下降的程度按比例增加。 如果不加以加强,它们的真正恢复显然会大为减少。 但是,如果价格的上涨是由于价值的提高,由于土地的肥力的提高而产生了这种供应,那么,判断任何金钱报酬应该增加多少比例,或者是否应该增加报酬,就是一个更美好的问题。改良和种植的延伸, 因为它必然会按照玉米价格的比例, 提高各种动物食品的价格, 所以它必然会降低, 我相信, 各种蔬菜食品的价格。 它提高了动物食品的价格;因为生产这种食品的很大一部分土地已经适合生产玉米,因此必须向房东反农民支付玉米土地的租金和利润。 它降低了蔬菜食品的价格;因为通过增加土地的肥力,它会增加其丰度.农业的改善也带来了许多种类的蔬菜食品,这些食品需要的土地更少,劳动力也不比玉米多,因此市场价格便宜得多。 这些是马铃薯和玉米,或称为印度玉米,这是欧洲农业的两个最重要的改进,欧洲本身也许已经从其商业和航行的大规模扩展中获得。 除此以外,许多种类的蔬菜食品,在粗鲁的农业状态下,都局限于厨房花园,只用 ⁇ 子饲养,在改良的状态下,来将菜引入普通田间,由犁头饲养;如萝卜,胡萝卜,卷心菜等. 因此,如果在改进过程中,一个食物品种的实际价格必然上升,另一个品种的价格必然下降;而判断一个品种的上涨在多大程度上可以由另一个品种的下跌来补偿,则变得更为温和。 当屠夫肉的实际价格一度达到其高度(对于每一种,除了猪肉之外,它似乎在一个多世纪前在英格兰的很大部分)时,任何以后在任何其他种类的动物食物中可能发生的涨价,都不会对人们低等阶层的情况产生很大影响.穷人的情况,通过英格兰的很大一部分,肯定不会因为家禽、鱼、野禽或野禽价格的上涨而感到如此痛苦,因为马铃薯的跌落必须使他们得到缓解。

p244.original: In the present season of scarcity, the high price of corn no doubt distresses the poor. But in times of moderate plenty, when corn is at its ordinary or average price, the natural rise in the price of any other sort of rude produce cannot much affect them. They suffer more, perhaps, by the artificial rise which has been occasioned by taxes in the price of some manufactured commodities, as of salt, soap, leather, candles, malt, beer, ale, etc.
p244.zh: 在目前这个缺粮的季节,玉米的高价格无疑使穷人感到痛苦。 但是,当玉米价格适中或平均价格低廉时,其他任何粗鲁产品价格的自然上涨都不会对它们产生多大影响。 也许,由于某些制成品价格的税收引起的人为上涨,他们遭受了更大的痛苦,如盐、肥皂、皮革、蜡烛、麦芽、啤酒、啤酒等。

p245.original: Effects of the Progress of Improvement upon the real Price of Manufactures.
p245.zh: 《改进制成品实际价格进展的影响》。

p246.original: It is the natural effect of improvement, however, to diminish gradually the real price of almost all manufactures. That of the manufacturing workmanship diminishes, perhaps, in all of them without exception. In consequence of better machinery, of greater dexterity, and of a more proper division and distribution of work, all of which are the natural effects of improvement, a much smaller quantity of labour becomes requisite for executing any particular piece of work; and though, in consequence of the flourishing circumstances of the society, the real price of labour should rise very considerably, yet the great diminution of the quantity will generally much more than compensate the greatest rise which can happen in the price.
p246.zh: 然而,改进的自然效果是逐步降低几乎所有制成品的实际价格。制造业的作风也许毫无例外地在所有这些方面都削弱了。 由于机械的改进、更灵活、以及工作分工和分配更适当,所有这些都是改进的自然结果,因此,执行任何特定工作都需要的劳动力数量要少得多;尽管如此,由于社会环境的繁荣,劳动力的实际价格应大幅上涨,但数量的大量缩减一般将远远超出对价格可能发生的最大上涨的补偿。

p247.original: There are, indeed, a few manufactures, in which the necessary rise in the real price of the rude materials will more than compensate all the advantages which improvement can introduce into the execution of the work in carpenters' and joiners' work, and in the coarser sort of cabinet work, the necessary rise in the real price of barren timber, in consequence of the improvement of land, will more than compensate all the advantages which can be derived from the best machinery, the greatest dexterity, and the most proper division and distribution of work.
p247.zh: 确有少数制造品,其中无礼材料实际价格的必要上涨,将超过补偿木匠和加入者工作上一切改进能给执行木匠和加入者工作带来的一切好处,在较粗的内阁工作上,由于土地的改良,贫木实际价格的必要上涨,将超过补偿从最好的机械,最大的弹性,最适当的分工和分配工作上能够得到的所有好处.

p248.original: But in all cases in which the real price of the rude material either does not rise at all, or does not rise very much, that of the manufactured commodity sinks very considerably.
p248.zh: 但是,在粗糙材料的实际价格要么根本没有上涨,要么没有大幅度上涨的所有情况下,制成品的汇兑量都非常大。

p249.original: This diminution of price has, in the course of the present and preceding century, been most remarkable in those manufactures of which the materials are the coarser metals. A better movement of a watch, than about the middle of the last century could have been bought for twenty pounds, may now perhaps be had for twenty shillings. In the work of cutlers and locksmiths, in all the toys which are made of the coarser metals, and in all those goods which are commonly known by the name of Birmingham and Sheffield ware, there has been, during the same period, a very great reduction of price, though not altogether so great as in watch-work. It has, however, been sufficient to astonish the workmen of every other part of Europe, who in many cases acknowledge that they can produce no work of equal goodness for double or even for triple the price. There are perhaps no manufactures, in which the division of labour can be carried further, or in which the machinery employed admits of' a greater variety of improvements, than those of which the materials are the coarser metals.
p249.zh: 在目前和上个世纪,价格的这种下降在材料为较粗金属的那些制造中最为显著。 比上个世纪中叶 更适合手表的移动 本来可以买20磅 现在也许可以买20先令 在刀工和锁匠的作品中,在用粗金属制成的所有玩具中,以及在以伯明翰和谢菲尔德·沃雷为人熟知的所有商品中,在同一时期,物价大幅下跌,虽然并没有像制表工作那样大. 然而,这足以震惊欧洲其他各地的工人,他们在许多情况下承认,他们无法为两倍甚至三倍的价格生产出同样善良的工作。可能没有制成品,其中分工可以进一步进行,或者所使用的机械比材料是较粗金属的机器更能接受各种各样的改进。

p250.original: In the clothing manufacture there has, during the same period, been no such sensible reduction of price. The price of superfine cloth, I have been assured, on the contrary, has, within these five-and-twenty or thirty years, risen somewhat in proportion to its quality, owing, it was said, to a considerable rise in the price of the material, which consists altogether of Spanish wool. That of the Yorkshire cloth, which is made altogether of English wool, is said, indeed, during the course of the present century, to have fallen a good deal in proportion to its quality. Quality, however, is so very disputable a matter, that I look upon all information of this kind as somewhat uncertain. In the clothing manufacture, the division of labour is nearly the same now as it was a century ago, and the machinery employed is not very different. There may, however, have been some small improvements in both, which may have occasioned some reduction of price.
p250.zh: 在服装制造方面,同期价格并没有如此合理。 相反,我得到的保证是,在这五、二十、三十年中,由于材料价格大幅上涨,即完全由西班牙羊毛组成的材料,其价格已按质量有所上升。约克郡的布料是完全用英国羊毛制成的,据说在本世纪期间,布布的品质已经下降。 然而,质量是一个非常有争议的问题,因此,我认为所有这类信息都有些不确定。 在服装制造方面,现在的劳动分工与一个世纪前差不多,所使用的机械没有太大的不同. 然而,这两方面都有一些小的改进,这可能导致价格的降低。

p251.original: But the reduction will appear much more sensible and undeniable, if we compare the price of this manufacture in the present times with what it was in a much remoter period, towards the end of the fifteenth century, when the labour was probably much less subdivided, and the machinery employed much more imperfect, than it is at present.
p251.zh: 但是,如果把这种制造在当今时代的价格与在更遥远的时期的价格进行比较,到15世纪末,劳动力的细分可能要少得多,机械的使用比现在更不完美,那么这种削减看来就更加合理和不可否认。

p252.original: In 1487, being the 4th of Henry VII., it was enacted, that "whosoever shall sell by retail a broad yard of the finest scarlet grained, or of other grained cloth of the finest making, above sixteen shillings, shall forfeit forty shillings for every yard so sold." Sixteen shillings, therefore, containing about the same quantity of silver as four-and-twenty shillings of our present money, was, at that time, reckoned not an unreasonable price for a yard of the finest cloth; and as this is a sumptuary law, such cloth, it is probable, had usually been sold somewhat dearer. A guinea may be reckoned the highest price in the present times. Even though the quality of the cloths, therefore, should be supposed equal, and that of the present times is most probably much superior, yet, even upon this supposition, the money price of the finest cloth appears to have been considerably reduced since the end of the fifteenth century. But its real price has been much more reduced. Six shillings and eightpence was then, and long afterwards, reckoned the average price of a quarter of wheat. Sixteen shillings, therefore, was the price of two quarters and more than three bushels of wheat. Valuing a quarter of wheat in the present times at eight-and-twenty shillings, the real price of a yard of fine cloth must, in those times, have been equal to at least three pounds six shillings and sixpence of our present money. The man who bought it must have parted with the command of a quantity of labour and subsistence equal to what that sum would purchase in the present times.
p252.zh: 1487年,作为亨利七世的第4位,它颁布,"凡通过零售出售最优秀的红线谷物或其他最优秀的谷物布的宽院子,超过16先令者,将没收每所出售的40先令",因此,16先令包含的银子数量与目前我们4和20先令的银子数量大约相同,在当时,它被算作是最优秀布的院子的不合理价格;而且由于这是一种假冒性的法律,这种布的销售量很可能是多少。豚鼠价格可能是目前最高的。 因此,即使布料的质量应该被假定是平等的,而现在的布料最有可能是优越的,然而,即使根据这种推测,最好的布料的货币价格似乎自15世纪末以来已经大大降低。 但是,它的实际价格已经大大降低。 当时,六先令和八便士,而且很长一段时间之后,估计了四分之一小麦的平均价格。 因此,16先令是2/4和3个以上小麦的价格。 在目前以8和20先令的价格估价四分之一的小麦,在那些时候,一院精美布的实际价格必须至少相当于我们目前钱的3磅6先令和6便士。购买它的人必须拥有相当于目前购买的数额的劳力和生活保障。

p253.original: The reduction in the real price of the coarse manufacture, though considerable, has not been so great as in that of the fine.
p253.zh: 粗制件实际价格的下降虽然相当大,但并没有像罚款那样大。

p254.original: In 1463, being the 3rd of Edward IV. it was enacted, that "no servant in husbandry nor common labourer, nor servant to any artificer inhabiting out of a city or burgh, shall use or wear in their clothing any cloth above two shillings the broad yard." In the 3rd of Edward IV., two shillings contained very nearly the same quantity of silver as four of our present money. But the Yorkshire cloth which is now sold at four shillings the yard, is probably much superior to any that was then made for the wearing of the very poorest order of common servants. Even the money price of their clothing, therefore, may, in proportion to the quality, be somewhat cheaper in the present than it was in those ancient times. The real price is certainly a good deal cheaper. Tenpence was then reckoned what is called the moderate and reasonable price of a bushel of wheat. Two shillings, therefore, was the price of two bushels and near two pecks of wheat, which in the present times, at three shillings and sixpence the bushel, would be worth eight shillings and ninepence. For a yard of this cloth the poor servant must have parted with the power of purchasing a quantity of subsistence equal to what eight shillings and ninepence would purchase in the present times. This is a sumptuary law, too, restraining the luxury and extravagance of the poor. Their clothing, therefore, had commonly been much more expensive.
